knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Work in the finite-dimensional Euclidean space \(\mathbb R^n\). For a nonempty polyhedron \(P\), let \(\operatorname{aff}P\) be its affine hull, \(\operatorname{rec}P:=\{d\mid x+td\in P\ \forall x\in P,\ \forall t\geq0\}\), and \(\operatorname{lin}P:=\operatorname{rec}P\cap(-\operatorname{rec}P)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition classifies nonempty finite-dimensional polyhedra by intrinsic dimension, boundedness, and lineality. Empty-set conventions are treated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polyhedral geometry regime is the data \(\mathcal R(P):=(k,\operatorname{rec}P,\operatorname{lin}P)\) associated with a nonempty set \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) admitting a finite halfspace representation \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n\mid Ax\leq b\}\), where \(k:=\dim(\operatorname{aff}P)\). The regime is full-dimensional when \(k=n\) and lower-dimensional when \(k<n\); bounded when \(\operatorname{rec}P=\{0\}\); pointed when \(\operatorname{lin}P=\{0\}\); pointed unbounded when \(\operatorname{lin}P=\{0\}\neq\operatorname{rec}P\); and nonpointed when \(\operatorname{lin}P\neq\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is classified by its intrinsic dimension \(k=\dim(\operatorname{aff}P)\), recession cone, and lineality space. It is full-dimensional if \(k=n\), lower-dimensional if \(k<n\), bounded if its recession cone is \(\{0\}\), pointed if its lineality space is \(\{0\}\), pointed unbounded if it has a nonzero recession direction but no lineality, and nonpointed if it has nonzero lineality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R(P)=\bigl(\dim(\operatorname{aff}P),\operatorname{rec}P,\operatorname{lin}P\bigr)\) determines the stated dimension, boundedness, pointedness, and lineality regimes.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(P=\{x\mid Ax\leq b\}\neq\varnothing\), then \(\operatorname{rec}P=\{d\mid Ad\leq0\}\) and \(\operatorname{lin}P=\{d\mid Ad=0\}\).
For nonempty closed convex \(P\), boundedness is equivalent to \(\operatorname{rec}P=\{0\}\), and containing no affine line is equivalent to \(\operatorname{lin}P=\{0\}\).
special_cases_latex: A polytope has regime \((k,\{0\},\{0\})\).
An affine subspace \(a+L\) has \(\operatorname{rec}(a+L)=\operatorname{lin}(a+L)=L\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every nonempty polyhedron belongs to exactly one of the bounded, pointed-unbounded, or nonpointed regimes.
The classifications by dimension and by recession behavior are independent: a lower-dimensional polyhedron may be bounded, pointed unbounded, or nonpointed.
boundary_notes: The recession cone is restricted here to nonempty sets, avoiding vacuous-quantifier conventions for the empty set.
Pointedness for a general polyhedron means absence of affine lines; for a cone \(K\), this is equivalent to \(K\cap(-K)=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the nonempty polyhedron.

children.title: Principal Polyhedral Classes
children.top_down_role: The affine, bounded, unbounded, and homogeneous objects of polyhedral analysis.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: All sets lie in \(\mathbb R^n\). A closed halfspace is a set \(\{x\mid a^Tx\leq\beta\}\), and a homogeneous halfspace has \(\beta=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a finite-dimensional taxonomy of affine sets, polyhedra, polytopes, and polyhedral cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The principal polyhedral classes are: (i) affine polyhedra \(M=\{x\mid Fx=g\}\); (ii) polyhedra \(P=\{x\mid Ax\leq b,\ Fx=g\}\), equivalently finite intersections of closed halfspaces and hyperplanes; (iii) polytopes \(Q=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_p\}\), equivalently bounded nonempty polyhedra; and (iv) polyhedral cones \(K=\{x\mid Ax\leq0,\ Fx=0\}\), equivalently finitely generated cones \(K=\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_q\}\). The empty set and \(\mathbb R^n\) are also polyhedral under the finite-intersection convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine polyhedron is the solution set of finitely many affine equations. A polyhedron is the solution set of finitely many weak linear inequalities and affine equations. A polytope is the convex hull of finitely many points, equivalently a nonempty bounded polyhedron. A polyhedral cone is a homogeneous polyhedron, equivalently the conic hull of finitely many vectors. The empty set and the whole space are included as polyhedral boundary cases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M=\{Fx=g\}\), \(P=\{Ax\leq b,Fx=g\}\), \(Q=\operatorname{conv}\{v_i\}_{i=1}^p\), and \(K=\{Ax\leq0,Fx=0\}=\operatorname{cone}\{r_j\}_{j=1}^q\) define the principal classes.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Every equality \(f^Tx=\gamma\) may be represented by the pair \(f^Tx\leq\gamma\) and \(-f^Tx\leq-\gamma\).
By Minkowski–Weyl, finite halfspace representability and finite point-and-ray generation define the same class of nonempty polyhedra.
special_cases_latex: A singleton is simultaneously an affine set and a polytope.
A linear subspace is an affine polyhedron and a polyhedral cone.
A simplex is the convex hull of a finite affinely independent set.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every polytope is closed and convex.
Every polyhedral cone contains the origin and is closed under nonnegative linear combinations.
boundary_notes: Some authors reverse the words “polyhedron” and “polytope”; this record uses “polytope” only for bounded polyhedra.
A general cone need not be convex or closed; a polyhedral cone has both properties.

notation.meaning: Convex hull of a finite point set.
Set of all nonnegative linear combinations of the listed generators.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A nonempty set \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a polyhedron if and only if there exist finite nonempty \(V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and finite \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) such that

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polyhedral cone is a set \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) representable as \[K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le 0\}\] for a finite matrix \(A\). Equivalently, there are finitely many vectors \(r_1,\ldots,r_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) such that \[K=\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_k\}=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i r_i:\lambda_i\ge 0\right\}.\] Thus polyhedral cones are precisely finitely generated convex cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral cone is an intersection of finitely many homogeneous halfspaces, equivalently the conical hull of finitely many generating directions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). For vectors \(r_1,\ldots,r_q\), write \(\operatorname{cone}\{r_j\}:=\{\sum_{j=1}^q\mu_jr_j\mid\mu_j\geq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closed convex cones are considered; finite inequality and finite generator descriptions are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a polyhedral cone if there exist finitely many vectors \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n\mid a_i^Tx\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\). Equivalently, there exist finitely many generators \(r_1,\ldots,r_q\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \(K=\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_q\}\). Its lineality space is \(\operatorname{lin}K:=K\cap(-K)\); it is pointed exactly when \(K\cap(-K)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral cone is an intersection of finitely many closed halfspaces whose boundary hyperplanes pass through the origin. By the conic Minkowski–Weyl theorem, this is equivalent to being generated by finitely many conic directions. Its lineality space consists of directions whose positives and negatives both belong to the cone, and the cone is pointed when this space is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K=\{x\mid Ax\leq0\}=\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_q\}\), with \(\operatorname{lin}K=K\cap(-K)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(K=\{x\mid Ax\leq0\}\), then \(\operatorname{lin}K=\ker A\).
A cone is polyhedral if and only if it is finitely generated.
special_cases_latex: The nonnegative orthant is \(\mathbb R_+^n=\operatorname{cone}\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\}\) and is pointed.
Every linear subspace is a nonpointed polyhedral cone unless it is \(\{0\}\).
The zero cone \(\{0\}\) is pointed and polyhedral.
immediate_consequences_latex: A polyhedral cone is closed and convex.
A pointed polyhedral cone has finitely many extreme rays and is generated by representatives of them.
boundary_notes: The displayed finite generating set need not be minimal and may contain redundant or zero generators.
For a nonpointed cone, lineality may be encoded by pairs \(\ell,-\ell\) in a conic generating list.

children.title: Affine-Dimension Geometry
children.top_down_role: Intrinsic dimension and affine data hidden or explicit in a representation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). An affine combination has the form \(\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_ix_i\) with \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition applies to arbitrary finite-dimensional sets and specializes to polyhedra; the empty set uses the conventional dimension \(-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine hull of \(S\) is \(\operatorname{aff}S:=\{\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_ix_i\mid m\geq1,\ x_i\in S,\ \lambda_i\in\mathbb R,\ \sum_i\lambda_i=1\}\), equivalently the smallest affine set containing \(S\). If \(S\neq\varnothing\) and \(x_0\in S\), then \(\operatorname{aff}S=x_0+\operatorname{span}(S-x_0)\), and its intrinsic dimension is \(\dim S:=\dim\operatorname{span}(S-x_0)\). By convention, \(\dim\varnothing=-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine hull of a set is the set of all finite affine combinations of its points, or equivalently the smallest affine set containing it. For any base point \(x_0\) in a nonempty set, its affine hull is the translate of the span of all differences \(x-x_0\). The dimension of the set is the dimension of this parallel subspace, independently of the chosen base point; the empty set has dimension \(-1\) by convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(S\neq\varnothing\) and \(x_0\in S\), \(\operatorname{aff}S=x_0+\operatorname{span}(S-x_0)\) and \(\dim S=\dim\operatorname{span}(S-x_0)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\dim S\) is the largest integer \(k\) for which \(S\) contains \(k+1\) affinely independent points when \(S\) is convex.
If \(\operatorname{aff}S=\{x\mid Fx=g\}\) with \(F\) having independent rows, then \(\dim S=n-\operatorname{rank}F\).
special_cases_latex: \(S\) is full-dimensional exactly when \(\operatorname{aff}S=\mathbb R^n\).
A singleton has dimension \(0\); a nondegenerate line segment has dimension \(1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Intrinsic dimension is invariant under injective affine transformations.
A polyhedron can have empty Euclidean interior while having nonempty relative interior in its affine hull.
boundary_notes: Ambient dimension \(n\) and intrinsic dimension \(\dim S\) need not agree.
The rank formula requires that the equations describe the affine hull, not merely a larger affine set containing \(S\).

notation.meaning: Set of displacement vectors \(\{x-x_0\mid x\in S\}\).

children.title: Intrinsic-Dimension Regimes
children.top_down_role: Intrinsic reformulation of full- and lower-dimensional polyhedra.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron, let \(M:=\operatorname{aff}P=x_0+L\), and put \(k:=\dim L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition distinguishes dimension relative to the affine hull from dimension in the ambient coordinate space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polyhedron \(P\) is full-dimensional in \(\mathbb R^n\) when \(k=n\), equivalently \(M=\mathbb R^n\), equivalently \(\operatorname{int}_{\mathbb R^n}P\neq\varnothing\). It is lower-dimensional when \(k<n\), in which case \(\operatorname{int}_{\mathbb R^n}P=\varnothing\) but \(\operatorname{ri}P\neq\varnothing\). An intrinsic-coordinate realization is obtained from any affine isomorphism \(T:\mathbb R^k\to M\); then \(\widehat P:=T^{-1}(P)\subseteq\mathbb R^k\) is a full-dimensional polyhedron and \(P=T(\widehat P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty polyhedron is full-dimensional when its affine hull is the whole ambient space, and lower-dimensional otherwise. A lower-dimensional polyhedron has empty ordinary interior but nonempty relative interior. Choosing affine coordinates on its affine hull produces a full-dimensional polyhedron in \(\mathbb R^k\), where \(k\) is its intrinsic dimension, and the original polyhedron is recovered by the affine coordinate map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k=n\iff\operatorname{aff}P=\mathbb R^n\iff\operatorname{int}P\neq\varnothing\), while \(k<n\) implies \(\operatorname{int}P=\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{ri}P\neq\varnothing\); moreover \(P=T(T^{-1}P)\) in intrinsic coordinates.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(M=\{x\mid Fx=g\}\) and the rows of \(F\) independently describe \(M\), then \(k=n-\operatorname{rank}F\).
For an affine isomorphism \(T:\mathbb R^k\to M\), \(T^{-1}(\operatorname{ri}P)=\operatorname{int}_{\mathbb R^k}(T^{-1}P)\).
special_cases_latex: A facet of a full-dimensional polyhedron in \(\mathbb R^n\) is intrinsically \((n-1)\)-dimensional.
A singleton is full-dimensional in its intrinsic space \(\mathbb R^0\), although lower-dimensional in every \(\mathbb R^n\) with \(n>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Statements requiring nonempty interior should be applied to a lower-dimensional polyhedron after restriction to its affine hull.
Redundant ambient coordinates do not alter intrinsic facial or recession geometry.
boundary_notes: An arbitrary parametrization of \(M\) must be injective to give intrinsic coordinates.
Ordinary interior and relative interior coincide only in the full-dimensional regime.

notation.meaning: Affine hull and its parallel linear subspace.

source_refs.locator: 1.5 Affine Sets and Convex Sets p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), its affine hull is \[\operatorname{aff}(C)=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i x_i:k\in\mathbb{N},\ k\ge 1,\ x_i\in C,\ \lambda_i\in\mathbb{R}\ (1\le i\le k),\ \sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i=1\right\}.\] It is the intersection of all affine sets containing \(C\). For every \(x_0\in C\), the associated direction space is \[\operatorname{par}(C)=\operatorname{aff}(C)-x_0=\operatorname{span}(C-x_0),\] and this linear space is independent of the choice of \(x_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine hull is the smallest affine set containing a nonempty set; translating it by any point of the set yields its intrinsic direction space.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Hull Geometry

source_witnesses.locator: 1.5 Affine Sets and Convex Sets p. 3

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Behavior of affine hulls and their parallel spaces under arbitrary affine maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and let \(T(x)=Mx+c\) be an affine map into \(\mathbb{R}^p\). Then \[\operatorname{aff}(T(C))=T(\operatorname{aff}(C)),\qquad \operatorname{par}(T(C))=M\operatorname{par}(C).\] No injectivity or surjectivity assumption on \(M\) is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine hulls commute with affine maps, and the parallel space of the image is the linear image of the original parallel space.
assumptions_latex: \(T(x)=Mx+c\) is an affine map from \(\mathbb{R}^n\) to \(\mathbb{R}^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{aff}(T(C))=T(\operatorname{aff}(C))\) and \(\operatorname{par}(T(C))=M\operatorname{par}(C)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Map Covariance of Affine Hulls

children.title: Intrinsic Dimension
children.top_down_role: Dimension measured relative to the affine carrier.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le\dim(C)\le n\), and \(\dim(C)\) is invariant under translations and invertible affine coordinate changes.

notation.meaning: Intrinsic or affine dimension of the set.
Direction space of the affine hull.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine dimension of a nonempty subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space.

source_refs.locator: 1.5 Affine Sets and Convex Sets p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), its intrinsic dimension is the linear dimension of the direction space parallel to its affine hull: \[\dim(C)=\dim\bigl(\operatorname{aff}(C)-x_0\bigr)=\dim\bigl(\operatorname{span}(C-x_0)\bigr),\qquad x_0\in C.\] This integer is independent of \(x_0\) and satisfies \(0\le\dim(C)\le n\). If \(T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) has the form \(T(x)=Mx+c\), where \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is invertible and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), then \(\dim(T(C))=\dim(C)\). Moreover, \(\dim(C)\) equals the maximum dimension of a simplex with affinely independent vertices in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The intrinsic dimension of a nonempty set is the dimension of the direction space parallel to its affine hull. It is unchanged by translations and invertible affine coordinate changes and equals the largest dimension of a simplex with vertices in the set.
knowledge_statements.title: Intrinsic Dimension

source_witnesses.locator: 1.5 Affine Sets and Convex Sets p. 3

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dimension-loss formula for arbitrary affine images.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, let \(T(x)=Mx+c\) map into \(\mathbb{R}^p\), and set \(L=\operatorname{par}(C)\). Then \[\dim(T(C))=\dim(M L)=\dim(C)-\dim(L\cap\ker M).\] Consequently \(\dim(T(C))\le\dim(C)\), with equality exactly when \(M\) is injective on \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine map reduces intrinsic dimension by the dimension of the affine carrier's directions annihilated by its linear part.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim(T(C))=\dim(C)-\dim(\operatorname{par}(C)\cap\ker M)\).

notation.meaning: Direction space parallel to the affine hull of \(C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension under Affine Maps

children.title: Full-Dimensional Regime
children.top_down_role: Polyhedra occupying the ambient affine space.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is full-dimensional exactly when \(\operatorname{aff}(C)=\mathbb{R}^n\), equivalently \(\dim(C)=n\), equivalently \(\operatorname{int}(C)\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean interior in the ambient space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambient full dimensionality for nonempty convex sets in \(\mathbb{R}^n\).

source_refs.locator: 1.5 Affine Sets and Convex Sets p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonempty convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is in the full-dimensional regime when its affine hull is the ambient space. The following conditions are equivalent: \[\operatorname{aff}(C)=\mathbb{R}^n,\qquad \dim(C)=n,\qquad \operatorname{int}(C)\ne\varnothing.\] In this regime, relative interior and Euclidean interior agree: \(\operatorname{ri}(C)=\operatorname{int}(C)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty convex set is full-dimensional precisely when its affine hull is the ambient space, or equivalently when it has nonempty Euclidean interior.
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Dimensional Regime

source_witnesses.locator: 1.5 Affine Sets and Convex Sets p. 3

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inequality-description criterion with zero-normal rows handled explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\ne\varnothing\). Then \(P\) is full-dimensional if and only if there exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) such that \[a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar x<b_i\qquad\text{for every }i\text{ with }a_i\ne0.\] Equivalently, no displayed inequality with a nonzero normal is an implicit equality. Zero-normal rows must be treated separately because a tautological row \(0^{\mathsf T}x\le0\) cannot be strict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty inequality-defined polyhedron is full-dimensional exactly when all inequalities with nonzero normals can be satisfied strictly at one common point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim(P)=n\iff\exists\bar x:\ a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar x<b_i\text{ for every }i\text{ with }a_i\ne0\).

notation.meaning: Common strict-feasibility point for all nonzero-normal rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Feasibility Test for Full Dimension

children.title: Lower-Dimensional Regime
children.top_down_role: Polyhedra confined to proper affine subspaces.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is lower-dimensional exactly when \(\dim(C)<n\), equivalently \(\operatorname{aff}(C)\ne\mathbb{R}^n\), equivalently \(\operatorname{int}(C)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Relative interior within the affine hull.
Euclidean interior in the ambient space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proper-affine-subspace regime for nonempty convex sets in \(\mathbb{R}^n\).

source_refs.locator: 1.5 Affine Sets and Convex Sets p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonempty convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is in the lower-dimensional regime when its affine hull is a proper affine subspace of the ambient space. Equivalently, \[\dim(C)<n,\qquad \operatorname{aff}(C)\ne\mathbb{R}^n,\qquad \operatorname{int}(C)=\varnothing.\] Although its Euclidean interior is empty, its relative interior within \(\operatorname{aff}(C)\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty convex set is lower-dimensional when its affine hull is proper; its ambient interior is empty, while its relative interior is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Dimensional Regime

source_witnesses.locator: 1.5 Affine Sets and Convex Sets p. 3

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic-coordinate representation of a lower-dimensional polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron of dimension \(r<n\). Choose \(x_0\in P\) and a matrix \(U\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) whose columns form a basis of \(\operatorname{par}(P)\). Then \[Q=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^r:x_0+Uz\in P\}\] is a full-dimensional polyhedron in \(\mathbb{R}^r\), \[P=x_0+UQ,\] and \(z\mapsto x_0+Uz\) is an affine bijection from \(Q\) onto \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine coordinates on a lower-dimensional polyhedron's hull represent it bijectively as a full-dimensional polyhedron in its intrinsic dimension.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(U\) form a basis of \(\operatorname{par}(P)\), and \(x_0\in P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=\{z:x_0+Uz\in P\}\) is full-dimensional in \(\mathbb{R}^r\) and \(P=x_0+UQ\).

notation.meaning: Basis matrix for the direction space of the affine hull.
Full-dimensional intrinsic-coordinate model of the polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Dimensional Affine Reduction

children.top_down_role: Equality structure encoded by an inequality description.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{aff}(P)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_Ix=b_I\}\).

notation.meaning: Indices of inequalities tight at every feasible point.
Submatrix and subvector indexed by the implicit equalities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine-hull equalities recoverable from a nonempty inequality description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\ne\varnothing\), and write the rows of \(A\) as \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\). An inequality indexed by \(i\) is an implicit equality when \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\) for every \(x\in P\). If \[I=\{i:a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\text{ for every }x\in P\},\] then the affine hull is represented by \[\operatorname{aff}(P)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_Ix=b_I\}.\] Redundant rows may make this equality system linearly dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inequalities that are tight at every feasible point form an equality system describing the affine hull of a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Equalities

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The implicit-equality representation is a nontrivial polyhedral result and fits the representation container, but no source or locator supports it.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Detection and Certification of Implicit Equalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rowwise linear-programming test, rational-input complexity, and Farkas certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each row \(i\), let \[s_i^*=\sup\{b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b\}.\] Row \(i\) is an implicit equality exactly when \(s_i^*=0\). Equivalently, it is implicit exactly when there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying \[A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=-a_i,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}\lambda\le-b_i.\] Thus all implicit rows can be detected using at most \(m\) linear programs; for rational input this is polynomial-time in the standard bit model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A row is implicit exactly when its maximum feasible slack is zero, equivalently when Farkas multipliers certify its reverse inequality; all rows can be tested with at most one LP each.
assumptions_latex: For the complexity assertion, \(A\) and \(b\) are rational and linear programs are solved in the standard bit model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i\in I\iff s_i^*=0\iff\exists\lambda\ge0:\ A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=-a_i,\ b^{\mathsf T}\lambda\le-b_i\).

notation.meaning: Farkas multiplier certifying validity of the reverse inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Detection and Certification of Implicit Equalities

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank formula for a nonempty inequality-defined polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\ne\varnothing\), and let \(I\) index all rows tight throughout \(P\). Then \[\dim(P)=n-\operatorname{rank}(A_I).\] Linearly dependent or repeated implicit rows do not change the value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine dimension of a nonempty inequality-defined polyhedron is the ambient dimension minus the rank of its implicit-equality rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim(P)=n-\operatorname{rank}(A_I)\).

notation.meaning: Submatrix formed from all implicit-equality rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension from Implicit Equalities

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact relative-interior description induced by implicit and nonimplicit rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\), let \(I\) be the indices of inequalities tight everywhere on \(P\). Then \[\operatorname{ri}(P)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_Ix=b_I,\ a_j^{\mathsf T}x<b_j\ \text{for every }j\notin I\}.\] In particular, all nonimplicit inequalities can be made strict simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relative interior consists exactly of points satisfying every implicit equality and strictly satisfying every remaining inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{ri}(P)=\{x:A_Ix=b_I,\ A_{I^c}x<b_{I^c}\}\).

notation.meaning: Interior of the polyhedron relative to its affine hull.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Interior from Nonimplicit Inequalities

children.title: Exceptional Polyhedral Cases
children.top_down_role: Boundary conventions needed for representations, faces, and polarity.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Work in \(\mathbb R^n\) and adopt the finite-intersection definition of a polyhedron. Recession and lineality are assigned only to nonempty sets in this record.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The record fixes conventions for the empty set, whole space, and zero-dimensional polyhedra, which otherwise create edge cases in dimension and representation statements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The exceptional polyhedral cases are normalized as follows. The inconsistent system \(0^Tx\leq-1\) represents \(\varnothing\), with \(\operatorname{aff}\varnothing=\varnothing\) and \(\dim\varnothing=-1\). The empty system represents \(\mathbb R^n\), with \(\operatorname{aff}\mathbb R^n=\mathbb R^n\), \(\operatorname{rec}\mathbb R^n=\operatorname{lin}\mathbb R^n=\mathbb R^n\). A nonempty zero-dimensional polyhedron is a singleton \(\{x_0\}\), with \(\operatorname{rec}\{x_0\}=\operatorname{lin}\{x_0\}=\{0\}\). Faces are taken to include \(\varnothing\) and the polyhedron itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The empty set is regarded as a polyhedron represented by an inconsistent finite system, has empty affine hull, and has dimension \(-1\). The whole space is the intersection of no constraints and has itself as affine hull, recession cone, and lineality space. Every nonempty zero-dimensional polyhedron is a singleton and has only the zero recession direction. Under the stated face convention, the empty face and the whole polyhedron are included among the faces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim\varnothing=-1\), \(\operatorname{rec}\mathbb R^n=\operatorname{lin}\mathbb R^n=\mathbb R^n\), and \(\dim P=0\neq P\Rightarrow P=\{x_0\}\) with \(\operatorname{rec}P=\{0\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\mathbb R^n\) is the intersection of the empty collection of halfspaces.
\(\varnothing\) can equivalently be represented by two inconsistent parallel hyperplanes.
special_cases_latex: When \(n=0\), the unique Euclidean space \(\mathbb R^0=\{0\}\) is simultaneously the whole space and a singleton.
For a nonempty polyhedron \(P\), the improper faces are \(\varnothing\) and \(P\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Claims about recession directions must state nonemptiness when the empty set is allowed.
Dimension induction can start at \(-1\) for \(\varnothing\) and at \(0\) for singletons.
boundary_notes: No recession cone is assigned to \(\varnothing\) here; defining it through a vacuous universal quantifier would produce a different convention.
Some authors exclude the empty set from the class of polyhedra or exclude improper faces; those conventions are not used here.

notation.meaning: The zero-dimensional vector space containing one point.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\varnothing\) exactly when the finite inequality system \(Ax\le b\) is infeasible.

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the inequality system.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empty-set case under the finite-intersection definition of a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An empty polyhedron is a polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(P=\varnothing\). In an inequality representation \[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\},\] emptiness means that no \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies all rows simultaneously. Thus emptiness is a property of the represented feasible set, not of any individual inequality, and different infeasible systems may represent the same empty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An empty polyhedron is the feasible set of an infeasible finite system of affine inequalities and is still admitted as a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty Polyhedra

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement is correct under the declared convention that empty finite inequality intersections are polyhedra, but that convention and its definition require an inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite inequality descriptions of the empty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\). Then \(P=\varnothing\) if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) such that \[y\ge0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y<0.\] Such a multiplier is an exact finite certificate of emptiness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality-defined polyhedron is empty exactly when a nonnegative linear combination of its inequalities has zero left-hand side and a strictly negative right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\varnothing\iff\exists y\ge0:\ A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y<0\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No invariant mathematical predicate for an “improper polyhedral object” can be fixed without an explicit local convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminology boundary: “improper” has incompatible meanings across convex and polyhedral settings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The phrase “improper polyhedral object” is not assigned a universal set-theoretic meaning by the basic definition of a polyhedron. Depending on context, exceptional objects may include \(\varnothing\), the whole space \(\mathbb{R}^n\), nonpointed cones, or extended-valued objects derived from improper convex functions. Consequently, any theorem using this phrase must explicitly declare the admitted class before properties such as dimension, recession, polarity, or facial structure are applied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: “Improper polyhedral object” is not canonical terminology; its meaning must be declared before dimension, recession, polarity, or face statements are interpreted.

children.title: Boundedness, Pointedness, and Lineality
children.top_down_role: Regimes separating vertex-dominated geometry from ray and lineality phenomena.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron. Define \(R:=\operatorname{rec}P\) and \(L:=R\cap(-R)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The taxonomy applies to nonempty finite-dimensional polyhedra and separates compact, ray-bearing, and line-bearing geometries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The boundedness–pointedness–lineality class of \(P\) is determined by the inclusions \(\{0\}\subseteq L\subseteq R\). The polyhedron is bounded exactly when \(R=\{0\}\); pointed exactly when \(L=\{0\}\), equivalently when it contains no affine line; pointed unbounded exactly when \(L=\{0\}\) and \(R\neq\{0\}\); and nonpointed exactly when \(L\neq\{0\}\). If \(P=\{x\mid Ax\leq b\}\), then \(R=\{d\mid Ad\leq0\}\) and \(L=\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty polyhedron, its recession cone contains all directions of infinite feasible motion and its lineality space contains the directions permitting motion in both signs. The set is bounded precisely when it has no nonzero recession direction. It is pointed precisely when it contains no line. Thus the three mutually exclusive regimes are bounded, pointed but unbounded, and nonpointed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(R=\{0\}\), \(L=\{0\}\subsetneq R\), or \(\{0\}\subsetneq L\subseteq R\) holds.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(d\in L\) if and only if \(P+d=P\), and then \(x+\mathbb Rd\subseteq P\) for every \(x\in P\).
A nonempty closed convex set is bounded if and only if its recession cone contains no nonzero vector.
special_cases_latex: Every bounded polyhedron is pointed.
A nonzero affine subspace is nonpointed.
A pointed polyhedral cone has the origin as its unique possible extreme point and has no nonzero subspace.
immediate_consequences_latex: A nonpointed nonempty closed convex set has no extreme points.
Writing \(P=L+(P\cap L^\perp)\) separates lineality from a line-free transverse polyhedron.
boundary_notes: Unboundedness alone does not imply nonpointedness: a ray is pointed and unbounded.
Pointedness does not imply full dimensionality or boundedness.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), define its recession cone by \[\operatorname{rec}(P)=\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:x+td\in P\text{ for every }x\in P\text{ and }t\ge0\}.\] Then \[P\text{ is bounded}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{rec}(P)=\{0\}.\] If \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\), then \(\operatorname{rec}(P)=\{d:Ad\le0\}\), so boundedness is equivalent to the homogeneous system \(Ad\le0\) having only the zero solution.

It is pointed and unbounded if and only if \(\operatorname{lin}(P)=\{0\}\) and \(\operatorname{rec}(P)\neq\{0\}\). In this regime, \(P\) has at least one vertex and admits finite sets \(V\subseteq P\) and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{rec}(P)\setminus\{0\}\) such that \[P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R).\] The nonzero vectors in \(R\) may be chosen along the extreme rays of \(\operatorname{rec}(P)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The regime contains unbounded polyhedra with rays but no affine lines.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polyhedron \(P\) has pointed unbounded geometry when \(R\neq\{0\}\) and \(L=\{0\}\). Equivalently, \(P\) is unbounded and contains no affine line. In this regime \(P\) admits a finite representation \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_p\}+\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_q\}\), where \(p\geq1\), at least one \(r_j\neq0\), and the recession cone \(R=\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_q\}\) is pointed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty polyhedron is pointed unbounded when it has at least one nonzero recession direction but no direction whose positive and negative both permit indefinite motion. Equivalently, it is unbounded but contains no line. Its Minkowski–Weyl representation has finitely many point generators and at least one ray generator, while the cone generated by the rays has zero lineality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\text{ pointed unbounded}\iff\operatorname{rec}P\neq\{0\}\text{ and }\operatorname{rec}P\cap(-\operatorname{rec}P)=\{0\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a nonempty closed convex set, absence of affine lines is equivalent to existence of an extreme point.
If \(P=\{x\mid Ax\leq b\}\), pointedness is equivalent to \(\ker A=\{0\}\), while unboundedness is equivalent to the existence of \(d\neq0\) with \(Ad\leq0\).
special_cases_latex: A ray \(x_0+\mathbb R_+d\) with \(d\neq0\) is pointed and unbounded.
A pointed polyhedral cone other than \(\{0\}\) is a pointed unbounded polyhedron.
immediate_consequences_latex: A pointed unbounded polyhedron has at least one vertex and finitely many vertices and extreme rays.
Its unboundedness is represented entirely by one-sided rays, never by a lineality subspace.
boundary_notes: Having a vertex does not imply boundedness.
A generating list may contain opposite rays redundantly; pointedness concerns the generated cone, not the syntax of a chosen list.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonpointed polyhedra and their lineality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron and let \(L=\operatorname{lin}(P)=\operatorname{rec}(P)\cap-\operatorname{rec}(P)\). Then \(P\) is nonpointed if and only if \(L\neq\{0\}\). If \(L\neq\{0\}\), then \(x+td\in P\) for every \(x\in P\), \(d\in L\), and \(t\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(P\) has no extreme points or vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedron is nonpointed exactly when it contains a nonzero lineality direction. In that case every point lies on a line contained in the polyhedron, so the polyhedron has no extreme points.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron, with \(R:=\operatorname{rec}P\) and \(L:=R\cap(-R)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This regime consists precisely of line-bearing nonempty polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polyhedron \(P\) has nonpointed geometry when \(L\neq\{0\}\). Equivalently, there exist \(x\in P\) and \(d\neq0\) such that \(x+td\in P\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\); indeed this then holds for every \(x\in P\). The lineality decomposition is \(P=L+(P\cap L^\perp)\), where \(P\cap L^\perp\) is a polyhedron containing no affine line.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty polyhedron is nonpointed exactly when its lineality space contains a nonzero vector. This means the polyhedron contains a full affine line and is invariant under translation by every lineality vector. It decomposes as the sum of its lineality subspace and a transverse polyhedron in the orthogonal complement that contains no line.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\text{ nonpointed}\iff L\neq\{0\}\iff\exists x\in P,\ d\neq0:\ x+\mathbb Rd\subseteq P\), and \(P=L+(P\cap L^\perp)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(d\in L\) if and only if \(P+d=P\).
If \(P=\{x\mid Ax\leq b\}\), then \(L=\ker A\), so nonpointedness is equivalent to \(\ker A\neq\{0\}\).

A strip such as \(\{x\in\mathbb R^2\mid0\leq x_1\leq1\}\) is nonpointed with lineality parallel to the \(x_2\)-axis.
immediate_consequences_latex: A nonpointed nonempty closed convex set has no extreme points.
A nonpointed polyhedron is necessarily unbounded.
boundary_notes: A polyhedron may be unbounded while pointed; nonpointedness specifically requires two-sided recession.
The transverse factor \(P\cap L^\perp\) depends on the selected inner product, although the quotient geometry modulo \(L\) does not.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition organizes external, generator, homogeneous, and lifted finite descriptions in finite-dimensional real spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite representation of \(P\) is any finite data system defining \(P\) in one of the equivalent polyhedral forms: an external form \(P=\{x\mid Ax\leq b,\ Fx=g\}\); a generator form \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_p\}+\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_q\}\) for nonempty \(P\); a homogeneous slice \(P=\{x\mid(x,1)\in K\}\) of a polyhedral cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}\); or a lifted form \(P=\{x\mid\exists y:\ A x+B y\leq c,\ F x+G y=h\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite representation describes a polyhedron using finitely many inequalities and equations, finitely many point and ray generators, a slice of a finitely generated homogeneous cone, or the projection of a polyhedron in a higher-dimensional space. These forms encode the same class of nonempty polyhedral sets, although their sizes and auxiliary variables may differ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite external, point-and-ray, homogeneous-slice, and lifted-projection descriptions all define polyhedral sets; every nonempty polyhedron has external, generator, and homogeneous-slice descriptions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Minkowski–Weyl gives \(\{x\mid Ax\leq b\}=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R\) for suitable finite \(V\neq\varnothing\) and \(R\).
A lifted form is the coordinate projection of the polyhedron \(Q:=\{(x,y)\mid Ax+By\leq c,\ Fx+Gy=h\}\).
special_cases_latex: A polytope requires no ray generators.
A polyhedral cone requires no affine normalization other than the homogeneous coordinate \(0\).
An ordinary external description is a lifted description with no auxiliary variable.
immediate_consequences_latex: Different finite representations of the same polyhedron need not have the same number of inequalities, generators, or auxiliary variables.
Linear images and coordinate projections of polyhedra are polyhedral.
boundary_notes: Equivalence concerns the represented set, not equality of the representation data.
The generator form displayed for nonempty sets does not directly represent the empty polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral and finitely generated convex sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite external and internal representations of convex sets in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is polyhedral convex if it is the intersection of finitely many closed half-spaces, equivalently if \[C=\{x:\langle x,b_i\rangle\leq\beta_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}.\] Consequently, every solution set of a finite mixed system of linear equations and weak linear inequalities is polyhedral, as is every affine set, including \(\varnothing\) and \(\mathbb R^n\). A polyhedral convex set is a cone if and only if it admits such a description with \(\beta_i=0\) for every \(i\). A convex set is finitely generated if it is the convex hull of finitely many points and directions: for some \(1\leq k\leq m\), its elements have the form \(x=\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i a_i\), where \(\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i=1\) and \(\lambda_i\geq0\). In the conic case \(k=0\), the normalization constraint is absent, so the set is generated by nonnegative combinations of finitely many vectors. The bounded finitely generated convex sets are the polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral convex set is an intersection of finitely many closed half-spaces. Finite mixed systems of linear equations and weak inequalities, including affine sets, therefore define polyhedral sets. Such a set is a cone exactly when it has a homogeneous inequality description. A finitely generated convex set is the convex hull of finitely many points and directions; a finitely generated cone consists of nonnegative combinations of finitely many generators. The bounded finitely generated convex sets are the polytopes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\text{ has the applicable finite half-space or point-direction representation; in the conic case the representation is homogeneous, and bounded finitely generated sets are polytopes.}

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(F\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(g\in\mathbb R^p\). Inequalities are componentwise.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: External representations describe finite-dimensional polyhedra as intersections of halfspaces and affine hyperplanes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An external representation of a set \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a finite system \((A,b,F,g)\) such that \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n\mid Ax\leq b,\ Fx=g\}\). Each row \(a_i^Tx\leq b_i\) specifies a closed halfspace and each row \(f_j^Tx=g_j\) specifies an affine hyperplane, so \(P\) is their finite intersection. Equality rows may be replaced by paired opposite inequalities without changing \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An external representation specifies a set by finitely many weak linear inequalities and affine equations. Geometrically, the represented polyhedron is the intersection of the corresponding closed halfspaces and hyperplanes. Equations can be encoded as pairs of opposite inequalities, so a pure finite halfspace description is equivalent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\{x\mid a_i^Tx\leq b_i\}\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^p\{x\mid f_j^Tx=g_j\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(Fx=g\iff Fx\leq g\text{ and }-Fx\leq-g\).
The representation is an inverse image \(P=(x\mapsto(Ax,Fx))^{-1}((-\infty,b]\times\{g\}))\), with the interval interpreted componentwise.
special_cases_latex: With \(m=0\), the representation defines an affine set.
With \(p=0\), it is a pure halfspace or H-description.
An inconsistent system represents \(\varnothing\), and the empty system represents \(\mathbb R^n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every externally represented set is closed and convex.
For nonempty \(P\), \(\operatorname{rec}P=\{d\mid Ad\leq0,\ Fd=0\}\).
boundary_notes: The same polyhedron generally has many external representations, including redundant ones.
Strict inequalities do not define closed polyhedra under this convention.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The H-representation is the pure finite-halfspace form; affine equations are encoded by paired inequalities when necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An H-representation of \(P\) is a finite pair \((A,b)\) satisfying \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n\mid Ax\leq b\}=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\{x\mid a_i^Tx\leq b_i\}\). A mixed representation \(Ax\leq b,\ Fx=g\) is converted to H-form by adjoining the rows \(F\) and \(-F\) with right-hand sides \(g\) and \(-g\). The representation is homogeneous precisely when \(b=0\), in which case it defines a polyhedral cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An H-representation is a description of a polyhedron as the intersection of finitely many closed halfspaces. Any affine equations can be included by replacing each equation with its two opposite weak inequalities. When every right-hand side is zero, all boundary hyperplanes pass through the origin and the represented set is a polyhedral cone.

Opposite proportional rows with matching right-hand sides can encode a hyperplane.
No rows gives \(\mathbb R^n\).

Feasibility, boundedness, and lineality are properties of the represented system but are invariant under replacement by an equivalent H-representation.

children.title: Standard-Form Slack-Lift Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Equality and nonnegativity descriptions in lifted spaces.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n\mid Ax\leq b,\ Fx=g\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). Introduce \(s\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The correspondence converts weak linear inequalities into affine equations plus nonnegativity in a lifted finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The slack lift of \(P\) is \(Q:=\{(x,s)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\mid Ax+s=b,\ Fx=g,\ s\geq0\}\). Its coordinate projection satisfies \(P=\{x\mid\exists s:\ (x,s)\in Q\}\), and the projection \((x,s)\mapsto x\) is bijective on \(Q\) because the unique slack associated with \(x\in P\) is \(s=b-Ax\). If nonnegative variables are required throughout, write \(x=x^+-x^-\) with \(x^+,x^-\geq0\), giving an equality-and-nonnegativity lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each inequality row, a nonnegative slack variable records the unused margin. The system \(Ax\leq b\) is therefore equivalent to the existence of \(s\geq0\) satisfying \(Ax+s=b\). Feasible points and lifted feasible points correspond one-to-one because the slack is uniquely \(b-Ax\). Splitting every unrestricted coordinate into the difference of two nonnegative variables yields a standard-form description using only equalities and nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in P\iff\exists!s\geq0:\ Ax+s=b,\ Fx=g\), where \(s=b-Ax\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(P=\pi_x(Q)\), where \(\pi_x(x,s)=x\).
With \(x=x^+-x^-\), \(P\) is the image of \(\{(x^+,x^-,s)\geq0\mid A(x^+-x^-)+s=b,\ F(x^+-x^-)=g\}\) under \((x^+,x^-,s)\mapsto x^+-x^-\).
special_cases_latex: If \(m=0\), no slack variables are needed.
An active inequality at \(x\) has slack component \(s_i=0\); a strict inequality has \(s_i>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The slack lift is a polyhedron in \(\mathbb R^{n+m}\).
Faces determined by active inequalities correspond to coordinate faces of the slack nonnegative orthant.
boundary_notes: The split \(x=x^+-x^-\) is not unique, unlike the slack vector associated with a fixed \(x\).
Slack lifting preserves the represented feasible set under projection but increases ambient dimension.

notation.meaning: Projection from the lifted space onto the original coordinates.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A standard-form polyhedron is a set \[Q=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^n:Az=b,\ z\ge0\},\] where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and the inequality is componentwise. Free variables can be replaced by differences of nonnegative variables, and finite inequalities can be converted into equalities by adjoining nonnegative slack variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise interpretation of canonical nonnegative slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the canonical slack lift \(Ax+s=b\), \(s\ge0\), every feasible pair satisfies \[s_i=b_i-a_i^\top x.\] Hence \[a_i^\top x=b_i\iff s_i=0,\qquad a_i^\top x<b_i\iff s_i>0.\] For any index set \(I\), points where all inequalities in \(I\) are active lift exactly to the coordinate section \(s_i=0\) for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slack coordinate is zero exactly for an active inequality and positive exactly for a strict inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_i^\top x=b_i\iff s_i=0,\qquad a_i^\top x<b_i\iff s_i>0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lifting of componentwise inequalities by nonnegative slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), and \(d\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and define \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b,\ Cx=d\}\). For \[Q=\{(x,s)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+m}:Ax+s=b,\ Cx=d,\ s\ge0\},\] where nonnegativity is componentwise, one has \[P=\pi_x(Q),\qquad \pi_x(x,s)=x.\] For each \(x\in P\), the compatible slack vector is uniquely determined by \(s=b-Ax\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding the uniquely determined nonnegative slack vector converts the inequalities into equalities, and projecting the lifted system onto the original variables recovers exactly the original polyhedron.

children.title: Lift Equivalence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometry Preserved by the Canonical Slack Isomorphism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Face, dimension, recession, lineality, and boundedness consequences of the canonical slack bijection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Cx=d\}\), let \(Q=\{(x,s):Ax+s=b,\ Cx=d,\ s\ge0\}\), and define \(\phi(x)=(x,b-Ax)\). The affine isomorphism \(\phi:P\to Q\) induces a dimension-preserving bijection \[F\longmapsto\phi(F)\] between the faces of \(P\) and \(Q\). Moreover, \[\operatorname{rec}(Q)=\{(v,-Av):v\in\operatorname{rec}(P)\},\qquad \operatorname{lin}(Q)=\{(v,-Av):v\in\operatorname{lin}(P)\}.\] Consequently, \(P\) and \(Q\) have the same dimension, are bounded simultaneously, and have corresponding vertices and face incidences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical slack bijection preserves the face structure, dimension, recession and lineality data, and boundedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\mapsto\phi(F)\text{ is a dimension-preserving face-lattice isomorphism, and }\operatorname{rec}(Q)=\{(v,-Av):v\in\operatorname{rec}(P)\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometry Preserved by the Canonical Slack Isomorphism

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\mapsto(x,b-Ax)\) is a bijection from \(P\) onto \(Q\), with inverse \(\pi_x\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bijection between an inequality system and its canonical slack lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b,\ Cx=d\}\] and \[Q=\{(x,s)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+m}:Ax+s=b,\ Cx=d,\ s\ge0\}.\] The affine map \(\phi:P\to Q\) defined by \(\phi(x)=(x,b-Ax)\) is bijective, and its inverse is the restriction of \(\pi_x(x,s)=x\) to \(Q\). Hence the original H-representation and its canonical slack lift describe affinely isomorphic feasible sets, despite occupying different ambient spaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row-wise primal witnesses and Farkas multiplier certificates for an external description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(a_i^\top x\le b_i\) and let \[Q_{-i}=\{x:A_{-i}x\le b_{-i},\ Cx=d\}\ne\varnothing.\] The row is redundant if and only if \[\sup_{x\in Q_{-i}}a_i^\top x\le b_i.\] Equivalently, it is redundant if and only if there exist \(\lambda\ge0\) and a free vector \(\mu\) such that \[A_{-i}^\top\lambda+C^\top\mu=a_i,\qquad b_{-i}^\top\lambda+d^\top\mu\le b_i.\] If it is not redundant, any \(x\in Q_{-i}\) satisfying \(a_i^\top x>b_i\) is a witness of necessity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality is redundant exactly when the remaining constraints imply it; this can be certified either by an optimization bound or by nonnegative Farkas multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_i^\top x\le b_i\text{ is implied by }Q_{-i}\iff\exists\lambda\ge0,\mu:\ A_{-i}^\top\lambda+C^\top\mu=a_i,\ b_{-i}^\top\lambda+d^\top\mu\le b_i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion-minimal inequalities relative to the affine hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b,\ Cx=d\}\neq\varnothing\), with \(Cx=d\) describing \(\operatorname{aff}(P)\). The inequality description is irredundant if and only if, for every row \(a_i^\top x\le b_i\), there exists \(x_i\in\operatorname{aff}(P)\) satisfying all other inequalities but \(a_i^\top x_i>b_i\). Equivalently, deleting any row strictly enlarges the represented set. Under irredundancy, each inequality defines a facet \[F_i=\{x\in P:a_i^\top x=b_i\}\] of \(P\) relative to \(\operatorname{aff}(P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An external description is irredundant when removing any inequality enlarges the polyhedron within its affine hull; each retained inequality then supports a relative facet.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The external description is irredundant when every listed inequality is indispensable: for each \(i\), \(\{x\in M\mid a_j^Tx\leq b_j\ \forall j\neq i\}\) strictly contains \(P\). Equivalently, for each \(i\) there exists \(x_i\in M\) satisfying \(a_j^Tx_i\leq b_j\) for all \(j\neq i\) but \(a_i^Tx_i>b_i\). An affine-equation subsystem is irredundant when its rows are independent and its solution set equals \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An external description is irredundant when deleting any one inequality strictly enlarges the represented set within its affine hull. Equivalently, every inequality has a witness that satisfies all the other constraints but violates that inequality. The equations describing the affine hull are required to be independent. For a polyhedron that is full-dimensional relative to its affine hull, each nontrivial inequality in such a description supports a facet.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The description is irredundant iff \(\forall i\ \exists x_i\in M:\ a_j^Tx_i\leq b_j\ (j\neq i)\) and \(a_i^Tx_i>b_i\).

children.title: Generator Representations
children.top_down_role: Internal descriptions by points, rays, and lineality directions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{v_1,\ldots,v_p\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(R=\{r_1,\ldots,r_q\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(L\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a linear subspace.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The representation applies to nonempty finite-dimensional polyhedra and explicitly separates bounded points, one-sided rays, and two-sided lineality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A generator representation of a nonempty polyhedron \(P\) is a finite description \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R+L\), meaning \(x\in P\) exactly when \(x=\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_iv_i+\sum_{j=1}^q\mu_jr_j+\ell\), where \(\lambda_i\geq0\), \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), \(\mu_j\geq0\), and \(\ell\in L\). The lineality term may be absorbed into the conic list by including \(\ell_k\) and \(-\ell_k\) for a basis \(\{\ell_k\}\) of \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generator representation expresses every point of a nonempty polyhedron as a convex combination of finitely many point generators, plus a nonnegative combination of finitely many ray generators, plus an arbitrary lineality vector. Conversely, every such finite point–ray–lineality expression defines a polyhedron. Lineality can alternatively be represented by including both signs of each basis direction among the ray generators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\left\{\sum_i\lambda_iv_i+\sum_j\mu_jr_j+\ell\mid\lambda\geq0,\ \mathbf1^T\lambda=1,\ \mu\geq0,\ \ell\in L\right\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Absorbing a basis of \(L\) with both signs gives \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}\widetilde R\).
In homogeneous coordinates, \(P=\{x\mid(x,1)\in\operatorname{cone}(\{(v_i,1)\}_i\cup\{(r_j,0)\}_j\cup\{(\pm\ell_k,0)\}_k)\}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(R=\varnothing\) and \(L=\{0\}\), then \(P=\operatorname{conv}V\) is a polytope.
If \(p=1\) and the point is \(0\), the representation describes a polyhedral cone.
For pointed \(P\), one may take \(L=\{0\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The recession cone is \(\operatorname{rec}P=\operatorname{cone}R+L\).
A finite generator representation determines a closed convex set and hence a polyhedron by Minkowski–Weyl.
boundary_notes: At least one point generator is required for a nonempty affine slice with coefficients summing to one.
Generator lists are generally nonunique and may contain nonextreme points, redundant rays, or lineality hidden as opposite rays.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, convex, and bounded. A point \(v\in P\) is a vertex, equivalently an extreme point, when \(v=(1-\lambda)x+\lambda y\), \(x,y\in P\), and \(0<\lambda<1\) imply \(x=y=v\). Write \(\operatorname{vert}(P)\) for the set of vertices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, nonempty, bounded polyhedra. The definition uses all vertices, not an arbitrary finite generating set containing redundant nonvertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vertex representation of \(P\) is the equality \[P=\operatorname{conv}(V)=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_i v^i:\lambda_i\geq0,\ \sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_i=1\right\},\qquad V=\operatorname{vert}(P)=\{v^1,\ldots,v^p\}.\] Thus every \(x\in P\) is a convex combination of vertices, and every listed generator is a vertex of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vertex representation writes a nonempty polytope as the convex hull of its finite set of vertices. Every point of the polytope is a convex combination of those vertices, and no listed point is merely a redundant nonvertex generator.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty bounded polyhedron.
\(V=\operatorname{vert}(P)\) denotes the set of all extreme points of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}(\operatorname{vert}(P))\), with \(\operatorname{vert}(P)\) finite.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every \(x\in P\), there exist \(\lambda_v\geq0\) for \(v\in\operatorname{vert}(P)\) such that \(\sum_v\lambda_v=1\) and \(x=\sum_v\lambda_vv\).
A set \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) admits such a finite vertex representation exactly when it is a nonempty bounded polyhedron.
special_cases_latex: If \(P=\{v\}\), then \(\operatorname{vert}(P)=\{v\}\).
If \(P\) is a line segment with distinct endpoints \(u,v\), then \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{u,v\}\) and these endpoints are its vertices.
immediate_consequences_latex: Any finite set \(W\) satisfying \(P=\operatorname{conv}(W)\) must contain every vertex of \(P\).
A linear functional attaining a unique maximum over \(P\) attains it at a vertex.
boundary_notes: The empty polytope is excluded because it has no nonempty convex-combination representation.
For unbounded polyhedra, vertices alone do not generate the set; recession directions are also required.
An arbitrary finite equality \(P=\operatorname{conv}(W)\) is a point-generator representation, but it is a vertex representation only when \(W=\operatorname{vert}(P)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generator Data Are Not Literally Unique Without Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness caused by scaling, lineality shifts, duplicate representatives, and changes of lineality basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a representation \[P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+L,\] the represented polyhedron is unchanged if a ray generator \(r\) is replaced by \(\alpha r\) with \(\alpha>0\), if a point or ray representative is shifted by an element of \(L\), or if a basis of \(L\) is replaced by another basis. Adding duplicate quotient-point or quotient-ray representatives also leaves \(P\) unchanged but destroys deletion irredundancy. Consequently, uniqueness claims for irredundant generator data are meaningful only modulo positive ray scaling, lineality, choice of lineality basis, and an explicit no-duplicate convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generator descriptions are nonunique under positive ray scaling, lineality shifts, basis changes, and duplicate representatives, so irredundancy requires explicit normalization conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Literal uniqueness of }(V,R,D)\text{ fails without quotient and normalization conventions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a nonempty polyhedron with lineality space \(L=\operatorname{lin}(P)\), let \(q:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n/L\) be the quotient map, and suppose \[P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+\operatorname{span}(D),\qquad \operatorname{span}(D)=L,\] with finite sets and \(q(r)\ne0\) for every \(r\in R\). Under deletion irredundancy and the convention that duplicate quotient point images and duplicate quotient rays are forbidden: (i) \(D\) is a basis of \(L\); (ii) \(q(V)\) is exactly the vertex set of \(q(P)\), with one lift for each vertex; and (iii) the rays \(\mathbb{R}_+q(r)\), \(r\in R\), are exactly the extreme rays of \(\operatorname{rec}(q(P))\), with one representative per ray. Conversely, data satisfying (i)–(iii) give a deletion-irredundant description under these conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After quotienting out lineality, irredundant point and ray generators are exactly the quotient vertices and extreme recession rays, while the lineality generators form a basis.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Work in \(\mathbb R^n\). An H-representation is \(P=\{x:Ax\leq b\}\) with finitely many inequalities. A finite generator representation is \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\) with finite \(V,R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real polyhedra, including bounded, unbounded, pointed, and nonpointed cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Minkowski–Weyl representation class consists of precisely those sets \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) for which the following equivalent finite descriptions exist: \[P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\leq b\}\] for some finite matrix–vector pair \((A,b)\), and \[P=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^p\}+\operatorname{cone}\{r^1,\ldots,r^q\}\] for finite point and direction sets. Lineality may be encoded by opposite rays or displayed separately as a linear-space summand.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minkowski–Weyl theory identifies the same finite-dimensional sets in two ways: intersections of finitely many affine halfspaces and sums of a finitely generated polytope with a finitely generated cone.
assumptions_latex: All constraint, point-generator, and ray-generator families are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) is a polyhedron if and only if \(P=Q+C\) for some polytope \(Q\) and finitely generated cone \(C\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(P\) is polyhedral if and only if there exist finite \(V,R\) with \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\).
The homogeneous specialization says that \(C=\{x:Ax\leq0\}\) if and only if \(C=\operatorname{cone}(R)\) for a finite \(R\).
special_cases_latex: If \(P\) is bounded, the cone summand is \(\{0\}\), yielding the polytope equivalence.
If \(P\) is a cone, the affine right-hand side is zero and no nonzero point component is needed.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every polyhedron has a finitely generated recession cone.
Finite linear images of polyhedra are polyhedra because generator descriptions are preserved by linear maps.
boundary_notes: The result is finite-dimensional; analogous statements require additional closure or compactness qualifications in infinite-dimensional spaces.
Neither the H-representation nor the generator representation is generally unique.
The empty-set convention requires separate handling because a convex hull generated by at least one point is nonempty.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous Minkowski–Weyl equivalence in finite dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a convex cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\), the following are equivalent: there exists a finite matrix \(A\) such that
\[
K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:Ax\le0\},
\]
and there exist finitely many vectors \(r_1,\ldots,r_m\in\mathbb{R}^d\) such that
\[
K=\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,
\ldots,r_m\}=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i r_i:\lambda_i\ge0\right\}.
\]
Thus a convex cone is polyhedral exactly when it is finitely generated; lineality may be represented by including generators for both directions of a line.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional convex cone has a finite homogeneous inequality description exactly when it has finitely many conic generators.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic Finite-Generation Equivalence

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Lift the positively weighted point generators to \((v_i,1)\) and ray generators to \((r_j,0)\). knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(d=\dim(\operatorname{aff}S)\), and let \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) lie in a linear subspace of dimension \(k=\dim(\operatorname{span}R)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Carathéodory sparsification replaces a representation by one with dimension-controlled support: \[x\in\operatorname{conv}(S)\Longrightarrow x=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_is^i,\quad m\leq d+1,\quad \lambda_i\geq0,\quad\sum_i\lambda_i=1,\] and, for conic combinations, \[y\in\operatorname{cone}(R)\Longrightarrow y=\sum_{j=1}^{t}\mu_jr^j,\quad t\leq k,\quad\mu_j\geq0.\] Zero coefficients are omitted, so the stated bounds concern active generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Carathéodory sparsification says that any point in a convex hull needs at most affine dimension plus one active point generators, while any point in a generated cone needs at most the dimension of the generator span active ray generators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convex representation of \(x\) uses at most \(d+1\) active points, and the conic representation of \(y\) uses at most \(k\) active rays.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In the ambient-dimension form, every \(x\in\operatorname{conv}(S)\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) uses at most \(n+1\) points.
The conic statement is equivalently a convex Carathéodory statement applied to an appropriate affine section whenever such a section meets every relevant ray.
special_cases_latex: In \(\mathbb R^2\), every point of a convex hull is a convex combination of at most three points.

immediate_consequences_latex: Every point of a polyhedron \(\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\) admits a representation using at most \(\dim(\operatorname{aff}V)+1\) active point generators and at most \(\dim(\operatorname{span}R)\) active ray generators.
The sparsity bound applies to each represented point and does not require reducing the global generator set.
boundary_notes: The bound is on active coefficients for one point, not on the total number of vertices or rays of the set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-sensitive finite representation in a generalized convex hull generated by points and directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be any set of points and directions in \(\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(C=\operatorname{conv}S\) in the generalized point-and-direction sense, and set \(d=\dim C\). Then \(x\in C\) if and only if \(x\) has a generalized convex representation using \(n+1\) elements of \(S\), not necessarily distinct. Moreover, \(C\) is the union of all generalized \(d\)-dimensional simplices whose vertices belong to \(S\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Homogenization, projection, and lifting operations for polyhedra
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\leq b\}\). Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+k}\) be a polyhedron in variables \((x,y)\), and let \(T\) be a linear map between finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional polyhedral sets and linear maps. The calculus records exact set correspondences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The homogenization–projection–lifting calculus consists of the operations \[\mathcal H(P)=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb R^{n+1}:Ax-bt\leq0,\ t\geq0\},\qquad P=\{x:(x,1)\in\mathcal H(P)\},\] \[\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\{x:\exists y\in\mathbb R^k,\ (x,y)\in Q\},\] and a lift of \(P\), namely any polyhedron \(Q\) with \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\), more generally \(P=T(Q)\). These operations convert affine descriptions to homogeneous ones and represent lower-dimensional polyhedra as linear images or sections of higher-dimensional polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenization embeds an affine polyhedron into a cone one dimension higher and recovers it at height one. Projection removes auxiliary coordinates existentially. A lifting is any higher-dimensional polyhedron whose projection or linear image is the original polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is linear when a general linear image is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\{x:(x,1)\in\mathcal H(P)\}\), and projections or linear images of finite-dimensional polyhedra are polyhedra.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The projection equation is the existential description \(x\in P\Longleftrightarrow\exists y\; Cx+Dy\leq e\).
A linear image \(T(Q)\) is a coordinate projection after adjoining equations \(x=Tz\).
special_cases_latex: For a cone \(P\), homogenization introduces no essential affine offset.
Taking \(k=0\) makes the lifting trivial: \(Q=P\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Finite extended descriptions remain within the class of polyhedra after eliminating auxiliary variables.
Homogenization permits affine polyhedral representation questions to be reduced to homogeneous conic questions.
boundary_notes: The slice \(t=0\) of \(\mathcal H(P)\) records recession directions rather than points of \(P\).
A projection representation need not be unique and may use many different auxiliary spaces.
The displayed homogenization convention includes \(t\geq0\); other conventions may take a closure of the positive hull of \(P\times\{1\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The homogenization of \(P\) is \[\mathcal H(P)=\{(z,t):Az-bt\leq0,\ t\geq0\}.\] Its height-one dehomogenization is \[\mathcal D(\mathcal H(P))=\{z:(z,1)\in\mathcal H(P)\}=P.\] More generally, if a cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}\) lies in \(t\geq0\), its height-one section is \(\mathcal D(K)=\{z:(z,1)\in K\}\); this section is polyhedral whenever \(K\) is polyhedral.

Affine polyhedral questions can be studied through homogeneous conic representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed homogenization retaining recession directions at height zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:Ax\le b\}\), define
\[
H(P):=\{(y,t)\in\mathbb{R}^{d+1}:Ay\le tb,\ t\ge0\}.
\]
Then \(H(P)\) is a polyhedral cone and
\[
H(P)=\overline{\operatorname{cone}(P\times\{1\})}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
H(P)\cap\{(y,t):t=1\}=P\times\{1\},
\qquad
H(P)\cap\{(y,t):t=0\}=\operatorname{rec}(P)\times\{0\}.
\]
Thus affine constants become coefficients of the homogenizing coordinate, while the zero-height slice records recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a nonnegative height coordinate converts affine inequalities into homogeneous ones; height one recovers the polyhedron and height zero its recession cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Homogenization of Affine Polyhedra

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Height-one dehomogenization for cones in the nonnegative-height halfspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}_+\) be a polyhedral cone with a nonempty height-one slice, and define
\[
P_K:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:(x,1)\in K\}.
\]
Then \(P_K\) is a polyhedron. Its recession cone is determined by the zero-height slice:
\[
\operatorname{rec}(P_K)=\{r\in\mathbb{R}^d:(r,0)\in K\}.
\]
If additionally \(K=\overline{\operatorname{cone}(K\cap(\mathbb{R}^d\times\{1\}))}\), then homogenizing \(P_K\) recovers \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty height-one slice of a nonnegative-height polyhedral cone is a polyhedron, whose recession cone is the zero-height slice.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalization by a Nonnegative Linear Functional
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-free dehomogenizing slices of closed cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a closed convex cone and let \(h\) be linear and nonnegative on \(K\). If \(B=\{z\in K:h(z)=1\}\) is nonempty, every ray \(\mathbb R_+z\) with \(h(z)>0\) meets \(B\) in the unique point \(z/h(z)\), and \[\operatorname{rec}(B)=K\cap\ker h.\] Thus rays annihilated by \(h\) are precisely the recession directions of the normalized slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative functional normalizes each positive-height ray once, while its zero-height cone is the slice's recession cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each ray with positive \(h\)-value meets \(B\) once, and \(\operatorname{rec}(B)=K\cap\ker h\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-height and zero-height slices of a homogenization cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=H(P)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d+1}\) be the homogenization cone of a nonempty polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\). For every \(t>0\), conicity and the height-one correspondence give
\[
K\cap(\mathbb{R}^d\times\{t\})=\{(tx,t):x\in P\},
\]
or equivalently
\[
\{y\in\mathbb{R}^d:(y,t)\in K\}=tP.
\]
At height zero,
\[
\{y\in\mathbb{R}^d:(y,0)\in K\}=\operatorname{rec}(P).
\]
Thus every positive slice is a scaled copy of \(P\), whereas the zero slice records its asymptotic geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-height slices of a homogenization cone are scaled copies of the original polyhedron; its zero-height slice is the recession cone.
