children.title: Extreme-Generator Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Conversion from external constraints to generators.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ Ex=f\}\) be a nonempty polyhedron, with lineality space \(L=\{d:Ad=0,\ Ed=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The output is geometric and irredundant up to positive rescaling of rays and choice of a basis for lineality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Extreme-generator enumeration is the H-to-V problem of producing all vertices \(V(P)\), one nonzero representative of every extreme ray of the pointed quotient recession cone \(\operatorname{rec}(P)/L\), and a basis of \(L\), so that \(P=\operatorname{conv}V(P)+\operatorname{cone}R(P)+L\). If \(P\) contains no lines, \(L=\{0\}\) and \(R(P)\) consists precisely of representatives of the extreme directions of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given linear constraints, extreme-generator enumeration outputs every vertex, one representative of each extreme recession ray after removing lineality, and a basis for the lineality space. These data reconstruct the polyhedron as a convex hull plus a conic hull plus lineality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}V(P)+\operatorname{cone}R(P)+L\), with \(V(P)\) and \(R(P)\) complete and nonredundant in the stated senses.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a pointed polyhedron, enumerate all zero- and one-dimensional proper faces representing vertices and extreme rays.
special_cases_latex: For a polytope, enumerate only vertices.
For a pointed polyhedral cone, enumerate only extreme rays; the origin is its unique vertex.
immediate_consequences_latex: The output is finite.
For full-dimensional polytopes, this is the vertex-enumeration problem.
boundary_notes: A polyhedron with lineality has no ordinary extreme points or extreme rays before quotienting by lineality.
Duplicate positive multiples do not represent distinct rays.

children.title: Vertex Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Recovery of extreme points from external polyhedral descriptions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is exactly \(\operatorname{vert}(P)\), without duplicates.

notation.meaning: Set of vertices of a polytope.
Rows active at a feasible point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite vertex enumeration from an inequality description of a bounded polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an inequality description \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\) of a polytope. Enumerate feasible candidates obtained from subsystems of active inequalities, or traverse adjacent bases. Retain a candidate \(v\) exactly when \(Av\le b\) and the active normals satisfy \(\operatorname{rank}A_{I(v)}=d\); merge duplicate candidates. Stop after every feasible basis or every vertex-adjacency state has been processed, and output the resulting set \(V\). Then \(V=\operatorname{vert}(P)\) and \(P=\operatorname{conv}V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate feasible full-rank active systems, remove duplicate solutions, and return precisely the vertices whose convex hull is the input polytope.
knowledge_statements.title: Vertex Enumeration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm classification fits the enumeration leaf, and the active-normal rank test is a standard vertex characterization for a polytope represented in the ambient space. No source with a specific locator supports the enumeration procedure or its completeness conclusion.

children.title: Extreme-Ray Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Recovery of extreme recession directions from external descriptions.

assumptions_latex: \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:Ax\le0\}\) is a pointed polyhedral cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output contains one nonzero representative of every extreme ray of \(K\).

notation.meaning: Ray generated by a nonzero vector.
Rows active at the ray generator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Enumeration of extreme rays of a pointed polyhedral cone from inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a pointed cone \(K=\{x:Ax\le0\}\). Generate nonzero feasible directions \(r\) from rank-defining active subsystems, normalize each candidate by a fixed convention, and retain it exactly when \(Ar\le0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}A_{I(r)}=d-1\). Remove positive scalar duplicates. Stop after all candidate active subsystems, or all adjacent extreme rays, have been processed. The output contains exactly one representative of each extreme ray \(\mathbb R_+r\) of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate normalized feasible directions whose active normals have rank one below full rank, obtaining one representative per extreme ray.
knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Ray Enumeration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is appropriately scoped to a pointed polyhedral cone and states the expected rank test and duplicate normalization. Its completeness and exact-one-representative conclusion require a cited authoritative enumeration source.

children.title: Pointed Polyhedron Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Enumeration behavior for polyhedra without nontrivial lineality.

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:Ax\le b\}\) is nonempty and pointed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The enumerated vertices and extreme rays give \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R\).

notation.meaning: Normalized representatives of recession-cone extreme rays.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined generator enumeration for nonempty pointed, possibly unbounded polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a nonempty pointed polyhedron \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\). Enumerate its vertices by feasible active systems of rank \(d\), and enumerate normalized extreme-ray generators of \(\operatorname{rec}P=\{r:Ar\le0\}\) by active systems of rank \(d-1\). Remove duplicates and stop when both finite enumerations are exhausted. With the resulting sets \(V\) and \(R\), output \((V,R)\). The representation is exact: \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a pointed polyhedron, enumerate vertices and recession-cone extreme rays; together they form an exact finite generator description.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointed Polyhedron Enumeration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm classification and pointed-polyhedron scope fit the leaf, and the generator conclusion has the correct form. No inspectable citation supports the combined vertex and recession-ray enumeration procedure or the exact representation claim.

children.title: Lineality-Sensitive Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Generator conversion in the presence of a nontrivial lineality space.

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:Ax\le b\}\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Enumeration modulo \(L\) yields \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R+L\).

notation.meaning: A linear complement of the lineality space.
Finite point and ray representative sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generator enumeration after separating the lineality space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a nonempty polyhedron \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\). Compute its lineality space \(L=\{r:Ar=0\}\), choose a complement \(W\) with \(\mathbb R^d=W\oplus L\), and enumerate the vertices and extreme recession rays of the pointed polyhedron represented in the quotient \(\mathbb R^d/L\), equivalently in \(W\). Lift representatives to finite sets \(V\) and \(R\), and output bases for \(L\) together with \((V,R)\). Then \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R+L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate lineality, enumerate point and ray generators in the pointed quotient, then lift them and add the lineality space.
knowledge_statements.title: Lineality-Sensitive Enumeration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm correctly separates lineality conceptually and fits the terminal container. A source is needed for the quotient-to-complement realization, lifting procedure, and exact generator representation, especially because these steps are only described at a high level.

children.title: Facet Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Conversion from generators to irredundant external descriptions.

assumptions_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R+L\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a nonempty polyhedron with finite generators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an irredundant equality-and-facet description of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a finite generator description into affine-hull equations and facet inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R+L\). Compute \(\operatorname{aff}P\), then generate supporting pairs \((a,\beta)\) satisfying \(a^Tv\le\beta\) for all \(v\in V\), \(a^Tr\le0\) for all \(r\in R\), and \(a^T\ell=0\) for all \(\ell\in L\). Retain one normalized pair exactly when its equality set has dimension \(\dim P-1\), and remove duplicates. Output affine-hull equations and the retained inequalities; their intersection is \(P\), and each retained inequality defines a facet.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find supporting inequalities valid on every generator, retain those exposing codimension-one faces, and output them with the affine-hull equations.
knowledge_statements.title: Facet Enumeration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and generator-to-facet conversion match the node role. The validity conditions and codimension-one contact criterion are plausible, but no source with a section, theorem, or page locator supports completeness or irredundancy of the output.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+L\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron, and let \(d=\dim P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facet inequalities are taken relative to \(\operatorname{aff}P\); affine-hull equations are reported separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Facet enumeration is the V-to-H problem of producing equations defining \(\operatorname{aff}P\) and one supporting inequality \(a_F^\top x\le\beta_F\) for every facet \(F\) of \(P\), where \(F=P\cap\{x:a_F^\top x=\beta_F\}\) and \(\dim F=d-1\). The output must satisfy \(P=\operatorname{aff}P\cap\bigcap_F\{x:a_F^\top x\le\beta_F\}\), and distinct output inequalities must define distinct facets, modulo positive scaling and addition of affine-hull equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facet enumeration converts point, ray, and lineality generators into an irredundant external description. It outputs the affine-hull equations and exactly one supporting inequality for each codimension-one face. Their intersection with the affine hull must equal the input polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{aff}P\cap\bigcap_{F\text{ facet}}\{x:a_F^\top x\le\beta_F\}\), with \(F=P\cap\{a_F^\top x=\beta_F\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For full-dimensional \(P\), enumerate the inequalities in an irredundant H-description.
Under polarity for suitable polytopes containing the origin, facet enumeration becomes vertex enumeration of the polar.
special_cases_latex: For a polytope, the input contains only point generators.
A zero-dimensional polytope has no facets under the codimension-one convention.
immediate_consequences_latex: The output is finite because a polyhedron has finitely many faces.
Every nonredundant inequality of a full-dimensional irredundant H-description defines a facet.
boundary_notes: Lower-dimensional affine-hull equations are not facet inequalities.
Positive scalar multiples define the same oriented half-space.

notation.meaning: A facet, namely a face of dimension d minus one.

children.title: Convex Hull Computation
children.top_down_role: Facet construction from finite point sets.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output describes exactly \(P=\operatorname{conv}V\) by affine-hull equations and facet inequalities.

notation.meaning: Convex hull of the input points.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of the external facet description of a finite point hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input finite nonempty \(V=\{v_1,\ldots,v_N\}\subseteq\mathbb R^d\). Compute \(H=\operatorname{aff}V\) and \(k=\dim H\). Generate normalized supporting pairs \((a,\beta)\) satisfying \(a^Tv_i\le\beta\) for every \(i\), and retain a pair exactly when \(\operatorname{aff}\{v_i:a^Tv_i=\beta\}\) has dimension \(k-1\). Remove duplicate supports and stop when all candidate supports have been processed. Output equations for \(H\) and the retained inequalities; their feasible set equals \(P=\operatorname{conv}V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute the affine hull and all supporting hyperplanes whose contact points span codimension-one faces, yielding exactly the hull's facet description.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Hull Computation

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Hull Computation as V-to-H Conversion
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(S=\{v_1,\ldots,v_N\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be finite and let \(P=\operatorname{conv}S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The target is an exact external description of a bounded polyhedron; lower-dimensional hulls are allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Convex hull computation takes \(S\) and returns equations \(Ex=f\) for \(\operatorname{aff}S\) together with facet inequalities \(Ax\le b\) such that \(\operatorname{conv}S=\{x:Ex=f,\ Ax\le b\}\). When an irredundant output is required, each row of \(Ax\le b\) defines a distinct facet of \(P\), and points of \(S\) that are not vertices may be omitted from the minimal V-description. Membership in the hull is equivalently \(x=\sum_i\lambda_iv_i\), \(\lambda_i\ge0\), \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex hull computation converts a finite point set into affine-hull equations and facet inequalities defining exactly its convex hull. In an irredundant output, each inequality represents one facet. The same set is characterized by convex-combination coefficients on the input points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}S=\{x:Ex=f,\ Ax\le b\}=\{\sum_i\lambda_iv_i:\lambda\ge0,\sum_i\lambda_i=1\}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a full-dimensional hull, the task is facet enumeration for a V-polytope.
The coefficient formulation is an extended formulation whose projection onto \(x\) is \(P\).
special_cases_latex: If all points coincide, the hull is a singleton.
If the points are affinely independent, the hull is a simplex.
immediate_consequences_latex: The hull is a polytope and therefore compact.
Only extreme input points are needed in a minimal generator description.
boundary_notes: Repeated or nonextreme input points do not change the hull.
Numerical orientation and degeneracy handling are outside this exact definition.

notation.meaning: Set of all convex combinations of points in S.

children.title: Face-Incidence Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Construction of face-lattice and adjacency information.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a polyhedron. A face is a set \(F=P\cap\{x:c^\top x=\delta\}\), where \(c^\top x\le\delta\) is valid for \(P\); include \(\varnothing\) and \(P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The output is the finite combinatorial structure of an exact polyhedron, not merely its vertex-edge graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Face-incidence enumeration produces the finite poset \(\mathcal F(P)\) of all faces ordered by inclusion. An incidence output may be represented by all pairs \((F,G)\) with \(F\subseteq G\), or minimally by cover relations \(F\lessdot G\), meaning \(F\subsetneq G\) and no face lies strictly between them. When facets and vertices are indexed, the vertex-facet incidence matrix has entry \(I_{vF}=1\) exactly when \(v\in F\). The complete cover relation determines the face lattice and its adjacency relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Face-incidence enumeration lists every face of a polyhedron and records inclusion, usually through cover relations. Vertex-facet incidence is the corresponding binary membership matrix. The full cover relation determines the finite face lattice, including vertex-edge and facet-ridge adjacency.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F(P)=(\{F:F\text{ is a face of }P\},\subseteq)\) is finite, and its cover relation determines all face incidences.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Two vertices are adjacent when their least containing face is one-dimensional.
Two facets are ridge-adjacent when their intersection is a face of codimension two.
special_cases_latex: For a simplex, the face lattice is the Boolean lattice on its vertices, with the empty face included.
For a polytope, every nonempty face is the convex hull of the vertices it contains.
immediate_consequences_latex: The vertex-edge graph and facet-ridge graph are induced substructures of the face lattice.
Incidence data are invariant under affine equivalence.
boundary_notes: Vertex-facet incidence alone may require closure operations to reconstruct all faces.
Improper faces must be handled consistently when reporting ranks.

notation.meaning: G covers F in the face poset.

children.title: Face Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Construction of polyhedral faces across selected dimensions or ranks.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a polyhedron given by a finite irredundant inequality description, with affine-hull equations separated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure outputs every nonempty face of \(P\) exactly once; the empty face may be added separately if required by convention.

notation.meaning: Face determined by making the indexed inequalities active.
Set of inequalities active throughout a nonempty face.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Enumeration of all nonempty faces from an irredundant external description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:Ax\le b,\ Ex=f\}\) with irredundant inequalities and affine-hull equations \(Ex=f\). Starting with \(P\), generate candidate faces by imposing equalities \(A_i x=b_i\). Discard empty candidates, replace each nonempty candidate \(F\) by its closure index set \(I(F)=\{i:A_i x=b_i\text{ for every }x\in F\}\), and merge candidates having equal closure sets. Continue until no new closure set occurs. Output the associated sets \(F_I\); these are exactly the nonempty faces of \(P\), including \(P\). Add the empty face separately if it is required by convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activate inequalities, discard empty intersections, canonicalize each nonempty face by its full active set, and output every nonempty face exactly once; add the empty face separately when required.
knowledge_statements.title: Face Enumeration

children.title: Face-Incidence Structure
children.top_down_role: Containment relations among vertices, edges, facets, or higher-dimensional faces.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a polyhedron with facets \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) and nonempty faces \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Containment among faces is encoded by reverse containment of their facet-incidence sets.

notation.meaning: Indices of facets containing a face.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding the face poset by incidences between faces and facets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonempty face \(F\) of a polyhedron \(P\) with facets \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\), define \(I(F)=\{i:F\subseteq G_i\}\). Then \(F=P\cap\bigcap_{i\in I(F)}G_i\), with the intersection interpreted through the corresponding supporting equalities. For faces \(F\) and \(H\), one has \(F\subseteq H\) if and only if \(I(F)\supseteq I(H)\). Thus the facet-incidence sets, ordered by reverse inclusion, represent the nonempty face poset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A face is determined by the facets containing it, and face containment corresponds to reverse containment of facet-incidence sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Face-Incidence Structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation content kind fits the structure leaf, and the reverse-inclusion encoding is stated consistently. No authoritative face-lattice source with a specific locator is cited for face determination by containing facets or for the order equivalence.

children.title: Face-Adjacency Structure
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood relations among faces of prescribed dimensions.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(H\) are distinct nonempty faces of \(P\) having the same dimension \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upper adjacency is characterized by \(\dim(F\vee H)=k+1\), while lower adjacency is characterized by \(F\cap H\ne\varnothing\) and \(\dim(F\cap H)=k-1\).

notation.meaning: Smallest face of the polyhedron containing both faces.
Affine dimension of a nonempty face.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper and lower adjacency relations between equal-dimensional faces in the graded face poset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) and \(H\) be distinct nonempty \(k\)-dimensional faces of a polyhedron \(P\). They are upper adjacent when their join \(F\vee H\), the smallest face containing \(F\cup H\), satisfies \(\dim(F\vee H)=k+1\). They are lower adjacent when \(F\cap H\ne\varnothing\) and \(\dim(F\cap H)=k-1\). Thus two vertices are upper adjacent exactly when their join is an edge, whereas two facets are lower adjacent exactly when their intersection is a ridge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal-dimensional faces have two distinct adjacency relations: upper adjacency means their smallest common containing face has dimension one greater, while lower adjacency means their nonempty intersection has dimension one less. Vertex adjacency is the upper relation, and facet adjacency through a ridge is the lower relation.
knowledge_statements.title: Face-Adjacency Structure

children.title: Face-Lattice Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Assembly of the graded combinatorial organization of a polyhedron.

assumptions_latex: All faces of \(P\), together with their dimensions and vertex sets, have been enumerated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting ordered set is the face lattice of \(P\).

notation.meaning: cover relation in the face poset

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports face-lattice reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconstruction from complete face and vertex-incidence data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form \(\mathcal F(P)\) by adjoining \(\varnothing\) and \(P\) to the enumerated proper faces. For \(F,G\in\mathcal F(P)\), set \(F\leq G\) exactly when the vertex set of \(F\) is contained in that of \(G\). Record a cover \(F\prec G\) when \(F<G\) and no enumerated face \(H\) satisfies \(F<H<G\). Output the Hasse diagram \((\mathcal F(P),\prec)\), with ranks \(\operatorname{rank}(F)=\dim F+1\), \(\operatorname{rank}(\varnothing)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order all enumerated faces by vertex-set inclusion, add the empty face and polytope, and retain only cover relations to obtain the face-lattice Hasse diagram.
knowledge_statements.title: Face-Lattice Reconstruction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and its content kind fit Face-Lattice Reconstruction, and vertex-set inclusion correctly orders faces of a polytope when complete face data are available. No cited source supports the reconstruction procedure or rank convention, so the record requires a specific inspectable source.

children.title: Representation-Conversion Method Families
children.top_down_role: Canonical conversion paradigms without procedural payload.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semantic Classification of Conversion Method Families
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathsf H(P)\), \(\mathsf V(P)\), and \(\mathsf F(P)\) denote external, generator, and face-incidence representations of the same polyhedron \(P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition classifies methods by maintained invariant and input-output relation; it intentionally omits procedural pseudocode.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A representation-conversion method family is a class of finite procedures sharing a conversion relation and a mathematical invariant. The canonical families are paired-description methods maintaining \(\operatorname{set}(H_i)=\operatorname{set}(V_i)\); traversal methods enumerating adjacent faces while preserving validity and nonrepetition; incremental hull methods maintaining \(P_i=\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_i\}\); and elimination or polarity reductions translating one conversion problem into projection or a dual conversion problem. A member is correct only when its terminal representation defines exactly the input polyhedron or its complete requested face set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representation-conversion methods are grouped by the invariant they maintain: paired constraints and generators, adjacency traversal, incremental hulls, or reductions through elimination and polarity. Correctness means that the terminal output represents exactly the input polyhedron or the complete requested incidence structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every method in the family maintains its stated invariant and terminates, when defined, with \(\operatorname{set}(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{out}})=\operatorname{set}(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{in}})\) or the complete requested face set.
special_cases_latex: Double-description methods are paired-description methods.
Reverse-search methods are traversal methods; incremental convex-hull algorithms are incremental methods.
immediate_consequences_latex: Different families may solve the same conversion relation while having different intermediate representations.
Polarity exchanges suitable vertex- and facet-enumeration tasks.
boundary_notes: This classification does not impose a uniform complexity bound.
A heuristic that can omit output objects is not a conversion method under this exact definition.

source_refs.locator: §3.17, Further Readings, Double Description Method, and Vertex Enumeration, pp. 120–123

review_flags: The source explicitly supports double-description and reverse-search families; the broader invariant-based taxonomy is a formal synthesis.

children.title: Double-Description Methods
children.top_down_role: Incremental maintenance of paired constraint and generator descriptions.

assumptions_latex: A new inequality \(a^Tx\leq\beta\) is to be inserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update produces paired constraint and generator descriptions of \(P_{k+1}=P_k\cap\{x:a^Tx\leq\beta\}\).

notation.meaning: generators satisfying, lying on, or violating the inserted inequality

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports double-description methods.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic incremental double-description update; implementation-specific filtering is abstracted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the current generators by the sign of \(a^Tv-\beta\). Retain generators in \(V^+\cup V^0\), using the convention \(V^+=\{v:a^Tv<\beta\}\). For each eligible adjacent pair \((u,v)\in V^+\times V^-\), insert the intersection point \(w=u+\lambda(v-u)\), where \(\lambda=(\beta-a^Tu)/(a^T(v-u))\). Apply the homogeneous analogue to rays, then delete redundant generators and append \(a^Tx\leq\beta\) to the constraint description. Stop after all inequalities have been inserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Insert inequalities one at a time, retain feasible generators, create boundary generators from eligible crossing pairs, and remove redundancies while maintaining both representations.
knowledge_statements.title: Double-Description Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits Double-Description Methods, but the stated point partition does not define the distinct homogeneous sign rule for rays, and the phrase "homogeneous analogue" is insufficient to determine the update for an unbounded polyhedron. Adjacency eligibility, lineality, and redundancy rules also require authoritative support before a mathematically reliable replacement can be made.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(R\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\), call \((A,R)\) an MW-pair when \(\{x:Ax\le0\}=\operatorname{cone}(R)\). Let \(A_i\) contain the first \(i\) rows of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The canonical homogeneous cone form is stated; general polyhedra may be homogenized before applying it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A double-description method incrementally maintains an MW-pair \((A_i,R_i)\). On adding the inequality \(a^\top x\le0\), partition columns \(r^j\) of \(R_i\) into \(J^+=\{j:a^\top r^j>0\}\), \(J^0=\{j:a^\top r^j=0\}\), and \(J^-=\{j:a^\top r^j<0\}\). Retain columns indexed by \(J^0\cup J^-\), and for each \((j,k)\in J^-\times J^+\) form \(r^{jk}=(a^\top r^k)r^j-(a^\top r^j)r^k\). After optional removal of nonextreme or duplicate columns, the new matrix \(R_{i+1}\) must satisfy \(\{x:A_{i+1}x\le0\}=\operatorname{cone}(R_{i+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A double-description method maintains both inequalities and generators of the same cone while adding constraints one at a time. Generators satisfying the new inequality are retained; pairs lying on opposite sides create boundary generators by a linear combination cancelling the new inequality. The updated generator cone must equal the updated constraint cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every stage, \((A_i,R_i)\) is an MW-pair, and finally \(\{x:Ax\le0\}=\operatorname{cone}(R_m)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(r^{jk}\) spans the ray in \(\operatorname{cone}(r^j,r^k)\cap\{x:a^\top x=0\}\).
special_cases_latex: For one initial half-space, generators may be chosen from \(-a\) and a basis of \(\{x:a^\top x=0\}\).
Homogenization converts vertex-and-ray enumeration for a polyhedron into cone-generator enumeration.
immediate_consequences_latex: The method gives a finite constructive H-to-V conversion.
Without adjacency and extremality filtering, one update may create \(|J^-||J^+|\) candidates.
boundary_notes: Candidate generators need not all be extreme and may require redundancy removal.
Intermediate and final generator counts can be exponential.

notation.meaning: Minkowski–Weyl pair of inequalities and cone generators.
Boundary generator formed from an opposite-sign pair.

source_refs.locator: §3.17, The Double Description Method, formula (3.10) and Lemma 3.51, pp. 120–122

children.title: Reverse-Search Methods
children.top_down_role: Enumeration through compact traversal of adjacency structures.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite connected adjacency graph.
A root \(r\in V\) and a parent map \(p:V\setminus\{r\}\to V\) are available.
Repeated application of \(p\) reaches \(r\) from every vertex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every vertex of \(G\) is output exactly once using storage proportional to traversal depth plus local adjacency data.
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports reverse search.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract reverse search on a finite polyhedral adjacency graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Output \(r\). At a current vertex \(v\), scan its neighbors in a fixed order and descend to a neighbor \(w\) precisely when \(p(w)=v\); output \(w\) upon descent. When no unvisited child remains, return to \(p(v)\), terminating after the root has no remaining child. Because the arcs \((w,p(w))\) form a rooted spanning tree, the traversal visits every \(v\in V\) exactly once without storing a global visited set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orient a connected adjacency graph toward a root with a parent rule, then depth-first traverse the induced tree to enumerate every object once.
knowledge_statements.title: Reverse-Search Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract rooted-tree traversal is consistent with reverse search, and algorithm is the correct content kind. The storage conclusion and its polyhedral-enumeration interpretation are nontrivial claims with no cited source or inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reverse Search on a Finite Adjacency Graph
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite connected undirected graph whose vertices are the objects to be enumerated. Assume that an adjacency oracle lists \(N(v)=\{w\in V:\{v,w\}\in E\}\), and fix a root \(r\in V\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exact enumeration from local adjacency and a deterministic parent rule; randomized traversal and approximate adjacency are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reverse-search structure on \(G\) is a map \(p:V\setminus\{r\}\to V\) such that \(p(v)\in N(v)\) for every \(v\ne r\), and for every \(v\in V\) there exists \(k\ge 0\) with \(p^{k}(v)=r\), where \(p(r)=r\) by convention. The directed arcs \((v,p(v))\) form an arborescence toward \(r\). Reverse search enumerates \(V\) by traversing the reverse arcs \(v\to w\) satisfying \(p(w)=v\), generating such children by scanning \(N(v)\). Each vertex is reported exactly once.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reverse-search method equips a finite connected adjacency graph with a root and a deterministic parent for every nonroot object. The parent must be adjacent and repeated parent steps must reach the root. The resulting parent arcs form a rooted spanning tree. Traversing these arcs in reverse, while testing adjacent objects to identify children, enumerates every object exactly once without storing the entire visited set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p(v)\in N(v)\quad(v\ne r),\qquad \forall v\in V\ \exists k\ge0:\ p^k(v)=r,\qquad V=\bigsqcup_{v\in V}\{v\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The functional digraph of \(p\), after adjoining \(p(r)=r\), has the unique directed cycle \((r)\); deleting that loop gives a spanning tree of \(G\) oriented toward \(r\).
A vertex \(w\) is a child of \(v\) precisely when \(w\in N(v)\) and \(p(w)=v\).
special_cases_latex: For polyhedral vertex enumeration, \(V\) may be the set of feasible bases or vertices and \(E\) the pivot-adjacency relation.
If \(G\) itself is a tree rooted at \(r\), the unique neighbor closer to \(r\) is the parent map.
immediate_consequences_latex: A depth-first implementation needs only the current root-to-vertex path plus local oracle state, rather than a global visited set.
Termination follows from finiteness of \(V\) and the requirement that every parent chain reaches \(r\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not itself bound the time needed to compute \(p(v)\), scan \(N(v)\), or test equality of represented objects.
If distinct encodings represent the same object, the graph must first specify whether vertices are objects or encodings; otherwise exact-once enumeration is not defined.

notation.meaning: Neighbors of vertex v in the enumeration graph.
Deterministic parent map directed toward the root.
The k-fold iterate of the parent map.

review_flags: No supplied local source was found that states the reverse-search parent-map definition and exact-once traversal with this scope.
knowledge_statements.title: Reverse Search on a Finite Adjacency Graph

children.title: Incremental Hull Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Progressive hull and facet construction.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb R^d\), and put \(P_k=\operatorname{conv}\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}\). Assume an initial index \(k_0\) is chosen so that \(P_{k_0}\) has the intended affine dimension and its facets and incidences are available.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional point-set hull construction using facet visibility; lower-dimensional inputs require computation in their affine hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An incremental hull method constructs \(P_{k+1}=\operatorname{conv}(P_k\cup\{a_{k+1}\})\) from a representation of \(P_k\). If \(a_{k+1}\in P_k\), the representation is unchanged. Otherwise, a facet \(F=\{x\in P_k:u_F^Tx=\beta_F\}\), with \(u_F^Tx\le\beta_F\) on \(P_k\), is visible when \(u_F^Ta_{k+1}>\beta_F\). The update deletes visible facets, retains nonvisible facets, and creates facets \(\operatorname{conv}(R\cup\{a_{k+1}\})\) over horizon ridges \(R\), namely ridges incident to both a visible and a nonvisible facet, subject to removal of redundant or coplanar descriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incremental hull algorithm inserts points one at a time. At each insertion it either detects that the new point already lies in the current hull or identifies the current facets visible from that point. Visible facets are removed, nonvisible facets remain, and new facets are formed by joining the new point to the horizon ridges separating visible from nonvisible facets. Redundant or coplanar facet descriptions are normalized after the update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P_{k+1}=\operatorname{conv}(P_k\cup\{a_{k+1}\}),\qquad \mathcal F_{k+1}=(\mathcal F_k\setminus\mathcal V_k)\cup\{\operatorname{conv}(R\cup\{a_{k+1}\}):R\in\mathcal H_k\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A facet is visible exactly when the new point lies strictly outside its supporting halfspace.
The horizon is the boundary, within the boundary complex of \(P_k\), of the union of visible facets.
special_cases_latex: For \(d=2\), visible edges form a boundary chain and the horizon consists of its two endpoint vertices.
When \(a_{k+1}\in P_k\), \(P_{k+1}=P_k\) and no combinatorial update is required.
immediate_consequences_latex: After all insertions, \(P_m=\operatorname{conv}\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\).
The insertion order changes intermediate hull sizes and work but not the final convex hull.
boundary_notes: Degenerate inputs may create nonsimplicial facets or multiple coplanar supporting facets, so a simplicial-only update rule is not part of this definition.
The definition specifies the update family, not a complexity guarantee for point location, visibility testing, or incidence maintenance.

notation.meaning: Facets of the current hull visible from the inserted point.
Horizon ridges between visible and nonvisible facets.
Facet set or normalized facet representation of the current hull.

review_flags: The supplied sources did not provide an inspectable locator for the incremental visible-facet and horizon-ridge update.
knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Convex-Hull Construction

children.title: Incremental Hull Construction
children.top_down_role: Progressive maintenance of hull or facet structure as generators are introduced.

assumptions_latex: A valid face representation of \(P_k=\operatorname{conv}\{x_1,\ldots,x_k\}\) is maintained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After the last insertion, the maintained representation describes \(\operatorname{conv}\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\).

notation.meaning: partial convex hull after k insertions

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports incremental hull construction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional incremental convex-hull construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with an affinely independent subset and its simplex hull \(P_k\). For each remaining point \(x_{k+1}\), first test membership in \(P_k\). If \(x_{k+1}\in P_k\), leave the hull unchanged. Otherwise identify the faces visible from \(x_{k+1}\), remove the visible boundary portion, and join \(x_{k+1}\) to the exposed horizon faces to obtain \(P_{k+1}=\operatorname{conv}(P_k\cup\{x_{k+1}\})\). Stop after every input point has been processed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a hull by inserting points, ignoring interior points and replacing the visible boundary by faces joining the new point to the horizon.
knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Hull Construction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record has the correct algorithmic role and matches incremental hull construction at a high level. The visible-boundary and horizon update, initialization outside the affine hull, and maintained face representation are not supported by a cited source.

children.title: Beneath–Beyond Construction
children.top_down_role: Visibility-based updating of facets during progressive hull construction.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is a full-dimensional polytope represented by its facets.
\(x\notin P\) is the next point, and all visibility tests are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated facets bound \(\operatorname{conv}(P\cup\{x\})\).

notation.meaning: facets visible from the inserted point

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports beneath–beyond construction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondegenerate facet-update form of beneath–beyond.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Classify each facet of \(P\) as visible from \(x\) when \(x\) lies strictly beyond its supporting hyperplane. Let \(\mathcal H_x\) be the ridges incident to both a visible and a nonvisible facet. Delete all facets in \(\mathcal V_x\); for every ridge \(R\in\mathcal H_x\), create the candidate facet \(\operatorname{conv}(R\cup\{x\})\), orient its supporting inequality inward, and discard duplicates or nonfacets. Retain every nonvisible old facet and output the resulting facet set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete facets visible from the new point and cone the new point over each horizon ridge, retaining the nonvisible old facets.
knowledge_statements.title: Beneath–Beyond Construction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind for Beneath-Beyond Construction. The facet-update description is plausible in a suitably nondegenerate regime, but the assumptions do not precisely state that regime, while duplicate, coplanar, and nonfacet handling is left abstract. A source is needed to establish the sufficient hypotheses and update rule.

children.title: Insertion-Order Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Combinatorial workload variation caused by the ordering of inserted generators.

assumptions_latex: A deterministic incremental hull algorithm processes a finite point set \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^d\).
Its intermediate work is determined by the faces of the partial hulls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Different insertion orders can yield different intermediate face counts and running times while producing the same final hull.

notation.meaning: number of faces of a polytope

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports insertion-order sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sensitivity of intermediate combinatorics, not of the final convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a permutation \(\pi\) of \(X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\), define \(P_k^{\pi}=\operatorname{conv}\{x_{\pi(1)},\ldots,x_{\pi(k)}\}\). Although \(P_n^{\pi}=\operatorname{conv}(X)\) for every \(\pi\), the sequence \(\bigl(f(P_k^{\pi})\bigr)_{k=1}^n\), and hence the number of visibility, adjacency, and face-update operations, need not be permutation invariant. Therefore insertion order is an algorithmic parameter even though it does not affect correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Point order does not change the final hull, but it can change partial hulls, intermediate face counts, and consequently the algorithm’s work.
knowledge_statements.title: Insertion-Order Sensitivity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Property is the appropriate content kind for insertion-order sensitivity, and the final hull is plainly permutation invariant. The asserted consequences for visibility, adjacency, face-update counts, and running time depend on the particular incremental algorithm and cost model, neither of which is specified or sourced.

children.title: Degenerate Incremental Regimes
children.top_down_role: Incremental construction under coplanarity, nonsimplicial faces, or repeated support events.

assumptions_latex: An incremental hull method maintains faces using sidedness and incidence predicates.
The input may contain affine dependencies, coplanar points, or points on existing faces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict visible–invisible classification alone is insufficient; degeneracy handling is required for a valid irredundant hull representation.
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports degenerate incremental regimes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for naive incremental face updates under degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x\in\partial P_k\), then \(x\) can lie on supporting hyperplanes of several incident faces without being strictly beyond any of them. Likewise, more than \(d\) input points may lie on one facet, so horizon ridges and candidate facets may be duplicated or non-simplicial. Consequently, an update based only on strict signs can omit incidences or retain duplicate faces. Correct implementations must use exact zero-sign handling together with symbolic perturbation, lexicographic rules, or explicit non-simplicial incidence maintenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coplanarity and boundary insertions make strict visibility tests ambiguous, so naive updates can lose incidences or duplicate faces unless degeneracy is handled explicitly.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Incremental Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure_boundary is the correct role for this terminal container. The degeneracy phenomena are plausible, but the claim that strict-sign updates omit incidences or retain duplicates and the listed sufficient resolution strategies require a source specific to degenerate incremental hull algorithms.

children.title: Traversal-Reduction Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Traversal and reduction methods based on bases, orbits, or subproblems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal O\) be a finite set of polyhedral objects to be produced, \(S\) a finite state space, and \(\pi:S\to\mathcal O\) a surjection. Let \(\sim\) be an equivalence relation on \(S\) identifying states representing the same object, symmetry orbit, basis class, or reduced subproblem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A unifying exact-enumeration definition for basis traversal, orbit reduction, and decomposition into canonically represented subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A traversal-reduction method consists of a connected state graph \(G_S=(S,E_S)\), a reduction map \(\rho:S\to S\), and a traversal rule such that \(\rho(s)\sim s\), \(\rho(\rho(s))=\rho(s)\), and \(s\sim t\Rightarrow\rho(s)=\rho(t)\). Thus \(R=\rho(S)\) contains exactly one representative of each equivalence class. The algorithm traverses only reduced states, or reduces every generated neighbor before duplicate suppression, and reports \(\pi(r)\) according to a specified output-equivalence rule. Completeness requires that the reduced transition graph induced by \(r\to\rho(t)\) for \(\{r,t\}\in E_S\) reaches every required representative from its root set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A traversal-reduction algorithm explores a graph of bases, orbit representatives, or subproblems while applying an idempotent canonical reduction. Equivalent states must reduce to the same representative, and every representative must remain reachable in the reduced transition graph. Outputs are attached to representatives using an explicit rule so that symmetry or redundant state descriptions do not cause omissions or uncontrolled duplication.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\rho(s)\sim s,\quad \rho^2=\rho,\quad s\sim t\Longrightarrow\rho(s)=\rho(t),\quad R=\rho(S)\cong S/{\sim}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The restriction of the quotient map \(S\to S/{\sim}\) to \(R\) is a bijection.
Canonicalization may occur before insertion into a traversal queue or after neighbor generation, provided transitions are interpreted in the reduced graph.
special_cases_latex: For basis traversal, states are feasible bases and \(\sim\) may identify bases defining the same degenerate vertex.
For symmetry reduction, \(\sim\) is membership in the same group orbit and \(\rho\) chooses one canonical orbit representative.
For decomposition, states are subproblems and reduction removes subproblems certified equivalent or dominated under the declared output rule.
immediate_consequences_latex: At most \(|R|\) canonical states need be retained for duplicate suppression.
Completeness is a reachability condition on the reduced graph, not merely on the unreduced state graph.
boundary_notes: A reduction that identifies states with different required outputs is invalid unless the output rule reconstructs the omitted outputs.
The definition supplies no polynomial bound for canonicalization, adjacency generation, or the number of reduced states.

notation.meaning: Map from traversal states to represented polyhedral objects.

review_flags: Traversal-Reduction Algorithm Family is an umbrella label; no inspected source stated this combined basis-orbit-subproblem definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Traversal with Canonical Reduction

children.title: Basis-Pivoting Methods
children.top_down_role: Traversal of polyhedral representations through adjacent bases or related local states.

assumptions_latex: Feasible bases and their adjacent pivots can be enumerated exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pivot traversal enumerates all reachable basic feasible solutions; deduplication maps them to the vertices of \(P\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports basis-pivoting enumeration.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertex enumeration through feasible-basis adjacency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an initial feasible basis \(B_0\). At a current feasible basis \(B\), enumerate admissible exchanges of one basic and one nonbasic index; solve the associated ratio test and retain exchanges producing feasible adjacent bases. Traverse the resulting basis graph using a visited-set or a canonical parent rule, outputting the basic feasible solution associated with each encountered basis. When degeneracy assigns several bases to the same vertex, identify equal solutions before output. Stop when no unexplored feasible pivot remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Traverse feasible bases by simplex-style pivots, convert each basis to its basic feasible solution, and deduplicate bases representing the same vertex.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Pivoting Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits Basis-Pivoting Methods. For the mixed equality-and-inequality representation, the record does not define the standard-form basis model, ratio test, or conditions ensuring that the traversed feasible-basis graph covers every vertex. These details cannot be validated without a specific source.

children.title: Symmetry-Reduction Methods
children.top_down_role: Use of group orbits to reduce equivalent faces, generators, or search states.

assumptions_latex: A finite group \(\Gamma\) acts on a finite polyhedral object set \(S\).
The action preserves the adjacency or incidence relation used for traversal.
Orbit equivalence and stabilizers can be computed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method outputs one canonical representative of each \(\Gamma\)-orbit in \(S\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports symmetry-reduced enumeration.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orbit-representative traversal under finite polyhedral symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select a seed \(s_0\in S\) and store \(\operatorname{can}(s_0)\). For each stored representative \(s\), generate its adjacent objects, replace every neighbor \(t\) by \(\operatorname{can}(t)\), and enqueue only canonical representatives not previously stored. Stabilizers may be used to generate one neighbor from each stabilizer orbit. Terminate when the queue is empty and output the stored representatives, optionally with orbit sizes \(|\Gamma|/|\operatorname{Stab}_\Gamma(s)|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonicalize objects under a finite symmetry group and traverse only unseen orbit representatives, optionally reducing neighbor generation with stabilizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Reduction Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and orbit-canonicalization theme fit Symmetry-Reduction Methods. Adjacency preservation alone does not ensure that traversal from one seed reaches every orbit unless the underlying object graph is connected or seeds cover all components. No source is supplied to resolve this missing coverage hypothesis or support the stabilizer reduction.

children.title: Polyhedral Decomposition Methods
children.top_down_role: Partition of conversion or enumeration problems into smaller polyhedral subproblems.

assumptions_latex: A polyhedron \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is expressed as a finite union \(P=\bigcup_{i=1}^m P_i\).
Each cell \(P_i\) is polyhedral and intersections \(P_i\cap P_j\) are common faces or empty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Locally computed objects, identified consistently on shared faces, reconstruct the corresponding global objects of \(P\).
review_flags: The precise decomposition objective is ambiguous from the node path.
No supplied locator supports the gluing conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local computation and gluing over a face-to-face polyhedral decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute the required faces, generators, or adjacency data separately on each cell \(P_i\). For every nonempty common face \(P_i\cap P_j\), identify local objects representing the same geometric face or generator and reconcile their incidences. Internal faces belonging only to the subdivision are removed when the desired output concerns \(P\) rather than the complex \(\mathcal C\). Completeness requires that every global object be represented in at least one cell and that all duplicate local representations be identified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve polyhedral tasks cell by cell, glue identical objects across common faces, and remove subdivision-only faces to recover global data.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Decomposition Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Principle is a plausible content kind for the terminal container, but "required" and "global" objects are not fixed, and local faces or generators do not in general become global objects merely by identifying duplicates and removing subdivision-only faces. A task-specific reconstruction criterion and supporting source are needed before the mathematical statement can be determined reliably.

children.title: Hybrid Traversal Architectures
children.top_down_role: Combined use of pivoting, orbit reduction, or decomposition within one computational framework.

assumptions_latex: A finite polyhedral search space has computable local adjacency.
A partition into subproblems and a canonical global identity test are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The architecture enumerates the global objects without omission and suppresses duplicates across local traversals.
review_flags: Hybrid architecture is underspecified by the node path.
No supplied locator supports this algorithmic formulation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic decomposition-plus-traversal enumeration architecture.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the search into \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\), select a seed for each nonempty subproblem, and run a local adjacency traversal within each \(S_i\). For every encountered object \(s\), compute a global key \(\kappa(s)\); output it only if that key has not appeared in another traversal. Boundary objects generate transfer tasks for adjacent subproblems according to a deterministic ownership rule. Terminate when all local queues and transfer queues are empty. Correctness requires coverage by the subproblems and connectivity of each locally traversed component from its seeds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine decomposition, local adjacency traversals, deterministic boundary ownership, and global canonical keys to enumerate objects without omissions or cross-subproblem duplicates.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Traversal Architectures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits Hybrid Traversal Architectures, but the search objects, subproblem boundaries, transfer relation, ownership rule, and global key are only schematic. The stated coverage and local-connectivity conditions do not by themselves formalize termination or omission-free enumeration, and no source supports this architecture.

children.title: Polyhedral Query Complexity
children.top_down_role: Structural diagnostics, encoding models, output sensitivity, and computational failure boundaries.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Schrijver, Theory of Linear and Integer Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Schrijver, Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an instance \(I\) encode one or more rational polyhedra in an explicitly declared representation. Let \(L(I)\) be its input encoding length, \(d(I)\) its ambient or affine dimension, and \(K(I)\) the encoding length of a requested output.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deterministic complexity classification; arithmetic-operation and approximate numerical models must be declared separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polyhedral query-complexity specification is a tuple \((\mathcal I,\mathcal R,Q,\mathcal M,\mu)\), where \(\mathcal I\) is an instance class, \(\mathcal R\) its representation scheme, \(Q:\mathcal I\to\mathcal Y\) a decision, search, optimization, counting, enumeration, or conversion query, \(\mathcal M\) a computational model, and \(\mu(I)=(L(I),K(I),d(I),\ldots)\) the size parameters. A complexity classification is meaningful only relative to this tuple: decision and search time are measured against input length and certificate size, whereas enumeration and conversion additionally distinguish preprocessing, delay, total time, output size, and working space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral query-complexity taxonomy fixes the represented instance class, the precise query, the computational model, and all size parameters before assigning a complexity label. It separates decision, search, optimization, counting, enumeration, and representation conversion. For output-producing tasks it records preprocessing, delay, total time, output length, and space, rather than treating input size as the only parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{Spec}(Q)=(\mathcal I,\mathcal R,Q,\mathcal M,\mu),\qquad \mu(I)=(L(I),K(I),d(I),\ldots).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Two complexity assertions concern the same formal problem only if their instance domains, accepted encodings, output semantics, and computational models agree.
An enumeration problem can be represented as a map \(Q(I)=(y_1,\ldots,y_{N(I)})\) together with an order-insensitive correctness relation and separate resource measures.
special_cases_latex: A feasibility query has Boolean output and may use a feasible point or infeasibility certificate.
An \(H\)-to-\(V\) conversion query has potentially exponential \(K(I)\), so input-polynomial and output-polynomial time are distinct notions.
immediate_consequences_latex: A polynomial arithmetic-operation count does not by itself imply polynomial bit complexity.
Complexity statements with fixed dimension are not interchangeable with statements in which dimension belongs to the input.
boundary_notes: The taxonomy does not assert that a particular polyhedral query belongs to any complexity class.
Numerical conditioning and tolerance-dependent approximate answers require parameters beyond rational encoding length.

notation.meaning: Bit length of the encoded input instance.
Bit length of the requested explicit output.

review_flags: No inspected source supplied a single authoritative definition covering the complete query and resource taxonomy.
knowledge_statements.title: Taxonomy of Polyhedral Computational Queries

children.title: Representation Validation Query Family
children.top_down_role: Decision and simplification tasks for represented polyhedra.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validation Queries for Explicit Polyhedral Representations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P_H=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:Ax\le b,8=Cx=e\}\) be an \(H\)-representation and \(P_V=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+L\) a generator representation, where \(L\) is a linear subspace.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact validation and simplification of finite rational representations; approximate equality under floating-point tolerances is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The representation-validation query family consists of decision or search maps that test whether a finite description denotes the claimed polyhedron and whether its entries are necessary. For an inequality \(a_i^Tx\le b_i\), redundancy means \(\{x:A_{-i}x\le b_{-i},Cx=e\}\subseteq\{x:a_i^Tx\le b_i\}\). For a generator \(v\in V\), redundancy means \(\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)+L=\operatorname{conv}(V\setminus\{v\})+\operatorname{cone}(R)+L\). Cross-representation validation asks whether \(P_H=P_V\), equivalently whether both inclusions hold. A simplification query returns an equivalent description containing no entry redundant under the selected representation semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representation validation covers exact questions about finite inequality, equation, vertex, ray, and lineality descriptions. It tests redundancy by deleting one entry and asking whether the represented set changes, tests equality of two descriptions by mutual containment, and may return an equivalent irredundant description. The semantics must distinguish points, rays, and lineality generators because their deletion criteria differ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[a_i^Tx\le b_i\text{ is redundant}\iff P_{H,-i}\subseteq\{x:a_i^Tx\le b_i\},\qquad P_H=P_V\iff(P_H\subseteq P_V\ \wedge\ P_V\subseteq P_H).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: An inequality is redundant exactly when removing it leaves the feasible set unchanged.
For nonempty \(P_{H,-i}\), redundancy of \(a_i^Tx\le b_i\) is equivalent to \(\sup\{a_i^Tx:x\in P_{H,-i}\}\le b_i\), with the extended-value convention.
special_cases_latex: Feasibility validation asks whether the represented polyhedron is empty.
Irredundancy validation returns true precisely when no tested inequality or generator can be removed without changing the represented set.
immediate_consequences_latex: Mutual containment reduces equality validation to two one-sided validation tasks.
A valid simplifier must preserve the represented set, not merely the optimum of one selected objective.
boundary_notes: Duplicate inequalities can both be individually redundant under some deletion conventions; the convention for simultaneous versus individual deletion must be fixed.
Minimal cardinality and irredundancy are different: an irredundant representation need not solve a globally minimal-description problem.

notation.meaning: The inequality system with row i deleted.
Point generators, recession-ray generators, and lineality subspace.

review_flags: No inspected source stated the combined inequality, generator, equality, and simplification query family at a precise locator.
knowledge_statements.title: Validation Queries for Explicit Polyhedral Representations

children.title: Polyhedral Membership Queries
children.top_down_role: Tests concerning whether a point belongs to a represented polyhedron.

assumptions_latex: Either an inequality or a generator representation of \(P\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The query returns whether \(y\in P\), with an explicit feasibility or violation certificate.
review_flags: Supplied convex-set locator is only indirectly relevant to computational membership certificates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact membership certificates for inequality and generator representations.

source_refs.locator: Outer Description of Closed Convex Sets p. 126
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms I: Fundamentals

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x:Ax\leq b\}\), membership holds exactly when every component of \(Ay-b\) is nonpositive; a row \(i\) with \(a_i^Ty>b_i\) certifies nonmembership. For \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\), membership holds exactly when there exist coefficients \(\lambda_v\geq0\) and \(\mu_r\geq0\) satisfying \(\sum_{v\in V}\lambda_v=1\) and \(y=\sum_{v\in V}\lambda_vv+\sum_{r\in R}\mu_rr\). Such coefficients certify membership; infeasibility of this linear system certifies nonmembership through a linear-separation certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Check all inequalities in an H-representation, or solve for convex and conic generator coefficients in a V-representation; violations or feasible coefficients are certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Membership Queries

source_witnesses.locator: Outer Description of Closed Convex Sets p. 126
source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms I: Fundamentals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Certificate is an appropriate content kind for this membership-query leaf, and the H- and V-representation membership conditions are mathematically standard. However, the cited locator on outer descriptions of closed convex sets does not specifically support the generator representation or the claimed computational certificates, and "infeasibility ... through a linear-separation certificate" does not state the dual certificate. A source with a specific locator covering polyhedral generator membership and Farkas/separation certificates is required.

children.title: Polyhedral Containment Queries
children.top_down_role: Tests concerning inclusion between represented polyhedral sets.

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\) and \(Q=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Cx\le d\}\), with rational data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\subseteq Q\iff \sup_{x\in P}c_j^{\mathsf T}x\le d_j\) for every row \(c_j^{\mathsf T}\) of \(C\).

notation.meaning: The polyhedron whose containment is tested.
Row defining the j-th inequality of Q.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Containment of two rational polyhedra given by inequality representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each inequality \(c_j^{\mathsf T}x\le d_j\) defining \(Q\), solve the linear optimization problem \(\sup\{c_j^{\mathsf T}x:x\in P\}\). Then \[P\subseteq Q\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sup_{x\in P}c_j^{\mathsf T}x\le d_j\ \text{ for every }j.\] Thus containment reduces to one linear-programming query per inequality of \(Q\). If \(P=\varnothing\), every inequality passes under the stated convention; if an objective is unbounded above, containment fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One polyhedron lies in another exactly when every defining inequality of the latter has maximum value at most its right-hand side over the former.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Containment Queries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The containment criterion is mathematically precise and the condition kind fits the query leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied for the LP reduction and edge-case conventions.

children.title: Constraint Redundancy Queries
children.top_down_role: Detection of inequalities or equalities removable from external descriptions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\) is redundant iff \(\sup_{x\in P_{-i}}a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\).

notation.meaning: System obtained after removing constraint i.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundancy in a finite inequality representation of a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inequality \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\) is redundant precisely when deleting it does not enlarge the represented set: \[P=P_{-i}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad P_{-i}\subseteq\{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sup_{x\in P_{-i}}a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i.\] Hence redundancy is decided by a linear program over the remaining constraints. Under \(\sup\varnothing=-\infty\), an inconsistent remaining system makes the deleted inequality redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint is redundant exactly when its maximum left-hand side over the other constraints does not exceed its right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Redundancy Queries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The redundancy criterion, including the empty-system convention, is correct and appropriately classified as a condition, but it has no citation.

children.title: Generator Redundancy Queries
children.top_down_role: Detection of dispensable points, rays, or lineality generators.

assumptions_latex: At least one generator remains after deleting \(v_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_i\) is redundant iff \(v_i\in\operatorname{conv}\{v_j:j\ne i\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite point generators of a polytope; ray redundancy requires a separate conic criterion.

source_refs.locator: 3 Convex Sets p. 49
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A point generator \(v_i\) is redundant when its deletion leaves the convex hull unchanged. Equivalently, \[\operatorname{conv}\{v_1,\ldots,v_m\}=\operatorname{conv}\{v_j:j
e i\}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad v_i=\sum_{j
e i}\lambda_jv_j\] for some coefficients satisfying \(\lambda_j\ge0\) and \(\sum_{j
e i}\lambda_j=1\). Feasibility of these linear equalities and inequalities is therefore a generator-redundancy query.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point generator is redundant exactly when it is a convex combination of the remaining generators.
