children.title: Polyhedral Uncertainty Sets
children.top_down_role: Finite polyhedral descriptions used to represent uncertain data.

assumptions_latex: The uncertain vector belongs to a finite-dimensional space \(\mathbb R^r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The set \(U\) is polyhedral, and its support function is the optimal value of a linear program.

notation.meaning: Support function of the uncertainty set
Direction in which support is evaluated

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional inequality representation, allowing bounded or unbounded uncertainty sets.

source_refs.locator: 7 Support Functions and Polar Sets p. 133
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A polyhedral uncertainty set is a nonempty set
\[
U:=\{u\in\mathbb R^r:Fu\le g\},
\]
where \(F\in\mathbb R^{s\times r}\) and \(g\in\mathbb R^s\). Its support function is
\[
\sigma_U(y):=\sup_{u\in U}y^{\mathsf T}u\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}.
\]
Thus evaluating worst-case affine dependence on \(u\) is a linear program. The set is a polytope precisely when it is bounded; boundedness guarantees that \(\sigma_U(y)\) is finite for every \(y\in\mathbb R^r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral uncertainty set is a nonempty solution set of finitely many linear inequalities; worst-case linear perturbations are its support-function values.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Uncertainty Sets

source_witnesses.locator: 7 Support Functions and Polar Sets p. 133
source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recession Criterion for Finite Worst-Case Values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finiteness domain of the support function of a nonempty polyhedral uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{u:Fu\le g\}\ne\varnothing\), with recession cone \(U^\infty=\{d:Fd\le0\}\). Then \[\sigma_U(y)<+\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y^{\mathsf T}d\le0\ \text{for every }d\in U^\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y\in(U^\infty)^\circ.\] If some \(d\in U^\infty\) satisfies \(y^{\mathsf T}d>0\), then \(\sigma_U(y)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worst-case linear value is finite exactly when its direction is nonpositive on every recession direction of the uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dom}\sigma_U=(U^\infty)^\circ.

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the uncertainty set
Polar cone of the recession cone

knowledge_statements.title: Recession Criterion for Finite Worst-Case Values

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vertex Representation of Bounded Polyhedral Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario representation of a polytope and its support function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the nonempty polyhedral uncertainty set \(U\) is bounded, then it has finitely many vertices \(v^1,\ldots,v^N\) and \[U=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^N\},\qquad \sigma_U(y)=\max_{1\le k\le N}y^{\mathsf T}v^k.\] Thus every worst-case linear perturbation over \(U\) is attained at a vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded polyhedral uncertainty set is the convex hull of finitely many vertices, and every linear worst case occurs at one of them.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) is nonempty, polyhedral, and bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^N\},\qquad\sigma_U(y)=\max_ky^{\mathsf T}v^k.
knowledge_statements.title: Vertex Representation of Bounded Polyhedral Uncertainty

children.title: Robust Polyhedral Counterparts
children.top_down_role: Deterministic polyhedral formulations induced by robust constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary of the Linear Robust-Counterpart Template
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which fixed-set affine LP dualization no longer guarantees a finite linear counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The standard linear counterpart obtained by dualizing \(\sup_{u\in U}(P^{\mathsf T}x)^{\mathsf T}u\) uses a fixed nonempty polyhedral set \(U\) and affine dependence on \(u\). If the inequalities defining \(U\) depend on \(x\), dualization can introduce products of decision variables and dual multipliers. If the uncertain expression is nonlinear in \(u\), its worst-case evaluation is not generally a linear program. Thus polyhedrality of each fixed uncertainty fiber alone does not guarantee a linear robust counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decision-dependent uncertainty or nonlinear dependence on the uncertain vector can destroy the standard finite linear counterpart.
assumptions_latex: The comparison is with the fixed-set, affine-uncertainty LP-dualization template.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Polyhedral uncertainty fibers alone do not guarantee a linear robust counterpart.}

notation.meaning: Dual multiplier that may couple bilinearly with x

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary of the Linear Robust-Counterpart Template

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite scenario formulation for a robust affine inequality over a polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^N\}\). Then \[(a_0+Pu)^{\mathsf T}x\le b\quad\text{for every }u\in U\] is equivalent to \[(a_0+Pv^k)^{\mathsf T}x\le b\qquad(k=1,\ldots,N).\] This formulation requires no multiplier variables, although its number of inequalities equals the number of listed vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For polytopal uncertainty given by its vertices, robust affine feasibility is exactly feasibility at every vertex.
assumptions_latex: The uncertain inequality depends affinely on \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall u\in U,\ (a_0+Pu)^{\mathsf T}x\le b\iff\forall k,\ (a_0+Pv^k)^{\mathsf T}x\le b.

notation.meaning: Vertex scenario of the uncertainty polytope

knowledge_statements.title: Vertex-Enumerated Robust Counterpart

assumptions_latex: The uncertainty set \(U=\{u:Fu\le g\}\) is nonempty.
For the fixed decision \(x\), the support value \(\sigma_U(P^{\mathsf T}x)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The semi-infinite robust constraint is equivalent to the existence of a finite-dimensional nonnegative dual certificate \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraintwise robust counterpart obtained from finite-dimensional linear-programming duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(P\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R\). The robust inequality
\[
(a_0+Pu)^{\mathsf T}x\le b\qquad\text{for every }u\in U
\]
is equivalent to
\[
a_0^{\mathsf T}x+\sigma_U(P^{\mathsf T}x)\le b.
\]
If \(U=\{u:Fu\le g\}\) is nonempty and the support value is finite, linear-programming strong duality gives the finite counterpart
\[
\exists\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^s:\qquad F^{\mathsf T}\lambda=P^{\mathsf T}x,
\qquad g^{\mathsf T}\lambda+a_0^{\mathsf T}x\le b.
\]
Thus a robust affine inequality over polyhedral uncertainty is represented by finitely many linear equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing the worst-case linear perturbation converts a robust affine constraint over a nonempty polyhedron into finitely many linear constraints with nonnegative multipliers.
knowledge_statements.title: Robust Polyhedral Counterparts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The robust-counterpart formula is mathematically plausible and the duality content kind fits the leaf, but no citation is supplied. Authoritative, inspectable locators are required for both the linear-programming strong-duality step and the robust polyhedral counterpart before the exact assumptions and equivalence can be accepted.

children.title: Discrete Polyhedral Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Continuous polyhedral approximations to discrete feasible sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering of linear-objective bounds under addition of valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq Q_2\subseteq Q_1\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), where \(Q_1,Q_2\) are polyhedra. For every linear minimization objective, \[\inf_{x\in Q_1}c^{\mathsf T}x\le\inf_{x\in Q_2}c^{\mathsf T}x\le\inf_{x\in X}c^{\mathsf T}x.\] Thus adding inequalities valid for \(X\) cannot weaken the relaxation bound. Equality with the discrete optimum for one objective does not imply \(Q_2=\operatorname{conv}X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tightening a relaxation with valid inequalities improves every minimization bound, but equality for one objective does not establish ideality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{Q_1}c^{\mathsf T}x\le\inf_{Q_2}c^{\mathsf T}x\le\inf_Xc^{\mathsf T}x.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonic Tightening of Polyhedral Relaxations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted polyhedral formulations whose projection supplies a relaxation in the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[R:=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{n+q}:Gx+Hy\le h\}\] be a polyhedron such that every \(x\in X\) has a lift \(y\) with \((x,y)\in R\). Then \[Q:=\operatorname{proj}_xR=\{x:\exists y,\ Gx+Hy\le h\}\] is a polyhedral relaxation of \(X\), and \[\inf_{(x,y)\in R}c^{\mathsf T}x=\inf_{x\in Q}c^{\mathsf T}x.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted polyhedron containing a lift of every discrete feasible point projects to a valid polyhedral relaxation with the same linear-objective bound.
assumptions_latex: For every \(x\in X\), some \(y\) satisfies \((x,y)\in R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}X\subseteq Q=\operatorname{proj}_xR,\qquad \inf_Rc^{\mathsf T}x=\inf_Qc^{\mathsf T}x.
knowledge_statements.title: Extended Polyhedral Relaxations

assumptions_latex: The mixed-discrete feasible set \(X\) is nonempty.
The relaxation \(Q\) is a polyhedron satisfying \(\operatorname{conv}X\subseteq Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimization over \(Q\) gives a valid linear-programming bound, and the relaxation is ideal exactly when \(Q=\operatorname{conv}X\).

notation.meaning: Convex hull of the discrete feasible set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral outer relaxations of finite-dimensional mixed-integer feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
X:=\{x\in\mathbb Z^k\times\mathbb R^{n-k}:Ax\le b\}.
\]
A polyhedron \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a polyhedral relaxation of \(X\) when
\[
\operatorname{conv}X\subseteq Q.
\]
For every \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), this inclusion yields the minimization bound
\[
\inf_{x\in Q}c^{\mathsf T}x\le \inf_{x\in X}c^{\mathsf T}x,
\]
with the usual extended-real conventions. The relaxation is called ideal when \(Q=\operatorname{conv}X\); then every linear objective has the same infimum over \(Q\) and \(X\), whenever either value is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral relaxation contains the convex hull of a mixed-discrete feasible set and supplies valid linear-programming bounds; it is ideal when it equals that hull.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Polyhedral Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and minimization bound are standard and internally consistent, and definition is an appropriate content kind for this leaf. However, the record has no source reference; an inspectable integer-programming or polyhedral-relaxation definition locator is required.

children.title: Integrality-Gap Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of polyhedral relaxations measured through separation from discrete optima.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-dependent gap conventions for a maximization relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a maximization problem with discrete optimum \(z_{\mathrm{IP}}(c)\) and relaxation optimum \(z_{\mathrm{LP}}(c)\ge z_{\mathrm{IP}}(c)\), define \[\Delta(c):=z_{\mathrm{LP}}(c)-z_{\mathrm{IP}}(c).\] When \(0<z_{\mathrm{IP}}(c)\le z_{\mathrm{LP}}(c)<+\infty\), define \[\Gamma(c):=\frac{z_{\mathrm{LP}}(c)}{z_{\mathrm{IP}}(c)}.\] This ratio convention is not meaningful when the integer optimum is zero, negative, or infinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The additive gap is the relaxation-value difference; the usual maximization ratio requires positive finite optimal values.
assumptions_latex: The multiplicative definition additionally requires \(0<z_{\mathrm{IP}}(c)\le z_{\mathrm{LP}}(c)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Delta(c)\ge0,\qquad \Gamma(c)\ge1\text{ whenever defined}.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive and Multiplicative Integrality Gaps

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive gaps are not invariant under positive rescaling of the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an objective \(c\) has \(0<\Delta(c)<+\infty\), then for every \(\alpha>0\), \[\Delta(\alpha c)=\alpha\Delta(c).\] Hence a scale-free uniform additive-gap bound cannot hold over an objective class closed under arbitrary positive scaling unless every objective in the class has zero gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero additive gap can be made arbitrarily large by rescaling the objective, so additive bounds require normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Delta(\alpha c)=\alpha\Delta(c).
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Boundary for Additive Gaps

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero-Gap Characterization of an Ideal Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: All-objectives characterization when the discrete convex hull is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C:=\operatorname{conv}X\) be nonempty and closed, and let \(Q\) be a nonempty closed convex set with \(C\subseteq Q\). Then \[Q=C\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \inf_{x\in Q}c^{\mathsf T}x=\inf_{x\in C}c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{for every }c\in\mathbb R^n.\] Thus every strict closed convex outer enlargement is exposed by at least one linear objective with a strict extended-real value gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the discrete convex hull is closed, a closed convex relaxation is ideal exactly when every linear objective has zero gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q=C\iff\forall c\in\mathbb R^n,\ \inf_Qc^{\mathsf T}x=\inf_Cc^{\mathsf T}x.

notation.meaning: Closed convex hull of the discrete feasible set

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Gap Characterization of an Ideal Relaxation

assumptions_latex: The comparison uses maximization with nonnegative finite optimal values.
For each \(n\ge2\), the relaxation is the edge relaxation of the stable-set problem on \(K_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The multiplicative integrality gap equals \(n/2\), so polyhedral relaxation alone gives no dimension-independent gap bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded multiplicative gap for the elementary edge relaxation of maximum stable set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(n\ge2\), consider
\[
z_{\mathrm{IP}}:=\max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i:x_i\in\{0,1\},\ x_i+x_j\le1\ \text{for }i\ne j\right\}
\]
and its polyhedral relaxation
\[
z_{\mathrm{LP}}:=\max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i:0\le x_i\le1,\ x_i+x_j\le1\ \text{for }i\ne j\right\}.
\]
Because every stable set of \(K_n\) has at most one vertex, \(z_{\mathrm{IP}}=1\). The point \(x_i=1/2\) is relaxation-feasible, and summing the pairwise inequalities shows \(z_{\mathrm{LP}}=n/2\). Hence
\[
\frac{z_{\mathrm{LP}}}{z_{\mathrm{IP}}}=\frac n2\longrightarrow+\infty.
\]
No uniform multiplicative integrality-gap bound follows merely from polyhedrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The edge relaxation for maximum stable set on a complete graph has ratio n/2, proving that polyhedral relaxations can have unbounded integrality gaps.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Gap Boundaries
